definition_en: a person who performs in plays or films; a person who takes part in an action or process
core_image: 一个人换上别人的衣服，站在灯光下成为另一个人
scene: 开机前导演把所有人叫到片场中央，只有那位主演还蹲在角落背台词。Before the first shot the director gathered everyone on set except the actor who was still learning his lines in the corner.
sceneCN: 这里 actor 指在影视作品中扮演角色的人（第 1 个义项：演员）；句意为开机前导演集合剧组，唯独主演还在角落里背台词。

derivatives.zh: 由 actor 加 -ess 构成，义为「女演员」
由 act 加 -ing 构成，义为「表演；演技」

senses.title: A performer of roles
senses.definition: a person whose job is to perform a character on stage or screen
senses.definitionCN: 以在舞台或屏幕上扮演角色为职业的人
senses.example: The actor spent two months learning the accent.
senses.exampleCN: 这位演员花了两个月学习那种口音。
senses.why: Latin actor meant a doer, and the stage turned that doer into a person who does someone else.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 actor 本指「做事的人」，舞台把它变成了「做另一个人」的人。

senses.title: A participant in an action
senses.definition: a person or group that takes part in and influences an event
senses.definitionCN: 参与并影响某一事件的人或群体
senses.example: The unions were key actors in the wage talks.
senses.exampleCN: 各工会是工资谈判中的关键行动者。
senses.why: Anybody who does something in a process can be called an actor, not only somebody on a stage.
senses.whyCN: 在任何过程中做事的人都能叫 actor，并不只限于舞台上的那一个。

intro.en: Actor is Latin for a doer, and only later did it mean a person who performs on stage.
intro.cn: actor 在拉丁语中意为「做事的人」，后来才专指在台上「做」别人的人。

items.en: Agere meant to do and to drive, the verb behind the whole family.
items.cn: agere 意为「做、驱动」，是整个词族背后的动词。

items.en: Actor was the agent noun: the one who does or drives.
items.cn: actor 是施动名词，指「做事或驱动的人」。

items.en: The participle actus named the deed itself, a doing completed.
items.cn: 分词 actus 指行为本身，即一次完成了的「做」。

items.en: French used the word for a doer and for a player on the stage.
items.cn: 法语用这个词兼指做事的人与舞台上的表演者。

items.en: English took it up, and the theatre sense gradually became the dominant one.
items.cn: 英语采纳了这个词，戏剧义逐渐成为主要用法。

note.en: The look-alike group is the act- family; the near-meaning group is the words for people who perform or take part.
note.cn: 形近组是 act- 词族；近义组是表示「表演者、参与者」的词。

entries.definition: To do something or play a role.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「行动；表演」。

entries.definition: The doing of something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「行动；举动」。

entries.definition: A woman who performs roles.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「女演员」。

entries.definition: A person who entertains an audience.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「表演者」，范围比演员更广。

entries.definition: A person who acts in a play.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「演员」，为较老的说法。

entries.definition: A person who takes part in an activity.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「参与者」，只强调参加。

normalIntro.en: The hooks follow the doer: on a stage, in a film, and inside any process.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子都围绕「做事的人」：在舞台上、在电影里、在任何过程里。

normal.en: Actor is the person noun of act, so it literally means the one who does.
normal.cn: actor 是 act 的人称名词，字面上就是「做的那一个」。

normal.en: An actor does another person on purpose; a participant only takes part.
normal.cn: actor 是故意去「做」另一个人；participant 只是参与其中。

normal.en: In reports and politics, actors are the groups that make things happen.
normal.cn: 在报道与政治里，actors 指真正推动事情发生的各方。

normal.en: The feminine actress is older in form and now often avoided in neutral writing.
normal.cn: 阴性形式 actress 出现较早，如今中性写作中常被避开。

normal.en: Remember the pair: act is the deed, actor is the doer of the deed.
normal.cn: 记住这一对：act 是那件事，actor 是做那件事的人。

abstract.en: A body in a borrowed coat, standing where the light falls.
abstract.cn: 一副身体穿着借来的外套，站在灯光落下的地方。

abstract.en: A face that changes owners every evening at eight.
abstract.cn: 一张每晚八点就换主人的脸。

abstract.en: A hand at a negotiating table, quietly moving the whole room.
abstract.cn: 谈判桌上的一只手，悄悄推动着整个房间。

examples.en: The actor refused to read the script before the first shoot.
examples.cn: 这位演员拒绝在首次拍摄前读剧本。

examples.en: Every actor in the scene had to learn the same dance.
examples.cn: 这场戏里的每位演员都得学会同一支舞。

examples.en: Small firms can be major actors in a local economy.
examples.cn: 小企业在地方经济中也能成为重要角色。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「艾克特」——艾克特别会演，一上台就换个人

root: 源自拉丁语 actor「做事者、驱动者」，由 agere「做、驱动」加施动后缀 -or 构成；经古法语 acteur 于十四世纪进入英语，先指做事的人，后以戏剧义为主；同根词有 act、action、actress。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses keep one idea: the person who does — either a role on a stage or a part in an event.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项守住同一个意思：做事的那个人——或在台上扮演角色，或在事件中担当一方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person wearing someone else's life for the length of a scene.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人在一场戏的时间里，过着别人的生活。

branches.en: THE STAGE: the doer becomes a character on cue.
branches.cn: 舞台线：做事的人在提示下变成一个角色。

branches.en: THE PROCESS: the doer becomes a force inside an event.
branches.cn: 事件线：做事的人变成事件中的一股力量。

branches.en: THE CAMERA: the same role is repeated for takes.
branches.cn: 镜头线：同一个角色要为不同镜头重复。

branches.en: THE VOICE: accent and breath are part of the doing.
branches.cn: 声音线：口音与呼吸也是「演」的一部分。

branches.en: THE TABLE: negotiators are actors in the plain sense.
branches.cn: 谈判桌线：谈判者用的是 actor 最朴素的那层意思。

intro.en: The root act- carries doing, and the agent suffix -or names the person who does.
intro.cn: 词干 act- 承载「做」，施动后缀 -or 指出做这件事的人。

latinIntro.en: Latin actor and actus are attested; English actor is recorded from the fourteenth century.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 actor 与 actus 均有文献可证；英语 actor 自十四世纪起有记录。

items.example: It supplies the doing inside actor.
items.exampleCN: 它提供 actor 内部那个「做」。

items.example: It is the source of actor.
items.exampleCN: 它是 actor 的来源。

items.example: It came into English almost unchanged.
items.exampleCN: 它几乎原样进入了英语。

items.example: It marks the person rather than the deed.
items.exampleCN: 它标记的是人，而不是那件事。

items.example: It forms actress.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 actress。

items.example: It forms acting, the art itself.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 acting，即表演这门技艺。

items.example: It forms actors.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 actors。

items.example: It forms action, the deed rather than the doer.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 action，指行为而非做事的人。

definition_zh: 实际的；真实的；确切数额的
definition_en: real and existing rather than imagined or expected; exact as opposed to estimated
core_image: 账本上划掉估算数字，改写成核对后的真实数目
scene: 预算表上先写的是估算数字，财务把每张发票核对一遍，才敢报出真正花掉的钱。The budget listed estimates, and finance reported the actual cost only after checking every invoice.
sceneCN: 这里 actual 指与估算相对的真实数额（第 2 个义项：确切的）；句意为财务核对全部发票后才报出实际成本。

derivatives.zh: 由 actual 加 -ly 构成，义为「实际上；竟然」
由 actual 加 -ity 构成，义为「现实；实际情况」
由 actual 加 -ize 构成，义为「实现；使成为现实」

senses.title: Real and existing
senses.definition: existing in fact rather than only in thought, plan or expectation
senses.definitionCN: 确实存在于事实中，而非只在想法、计划或预期里
senses.example: The actual damage was far worse than the report suggested.
senses.exampleCN: 实际损失远比报告所暗示的严重。
senses.why: The Latin source means done, so what is actual has already been done and can be pointed at.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词源意为「已做成」，所以 actual 的东西是已经发生、能被指认的。

senses.title: Exact rather than estimated
senses.definition: given as an exact figure instead of a guess or round number
senses.definitionCN: 以精确数字给出，而非猜测或约数
senses.example: We need the actual number of visitors, not a rough guess.
senses.exampleCN: 我们要访客的确切数字，不要粗略估计。
senses.why: A figure that has been established is a figure that has been done, and the adjective marks it.
senses.whyCN: 已经被核定的数字就是「做成了」的数字，这个形容词正好标记它。

intro.en: Actual comes from a Latin word for done and entered English as the adjective of deeds, later contrasting with the merely imagined.
intro.cn: actual 出自拉丁语表示「已做成」的词，进入英语时是「行为」的形容词，后来专与「只是想象」相对。

items.en: Agere meant to do and to set in motion.
items.cn: agere 意为「做、使动起来」。

items.en: Actus, a doing, gave the stem from which the adjective was formed.
items.cn: actus 表示「一次做」，提供了构成该形容词的词干。

items.en: Actualis described something that exists in act, not only in capacity.
items.cn: actualis 形容以「行动」形式存在的东西，而不只是潜在能力。

items.en: French used it for what is real and in force at the moment.
items.cn: 法语用它指当下真实而有效的东西。

items.en: English adopted it for real deeds and facts, and later for exact figures.
items.cn: 英语用它指真实的行为与事实，后来又用于确切数字。

note.en: The look-alike group is the act- family; the near-meaning group is the adjectives of truth.
note.cn: 形近组是 act- 词族；近义组是表示「真实」的形容词。

entries.definition: The state of being real.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「现实；实际情况」。

entries.definition: In fact; really.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「实际上；竟然」。

entries.definition: To do something or perform a role.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「行动；表演」。

entries.definition: Existing in the world, not imagined.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「真实的」，最通用。

entries.definition: Truly what it claims to be, not fake.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「真正的」，强调非伪造。

entries.definition: Based on facts and correct.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「事实的；符合事实的」。

normalIntro.en: The hooks set actual against the imagined, the expected, and the rounded.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把 actual 与想象、预期和约数一一对立起来。

normal.en: Actual comes from done, so it points at what has really happened.
normal.cn: actual 出自「已做成」，所以它指向真正发生过的事。

normal.en: In actual fact is a set phrase that pushes a claim toward reality.
normal.cn: in actual fact 是固定说法，把一句主张推向现实。

normal.en: Actual size on a drawing means the drawing is as big as the object.
normal.cn: 图纸上的 actual size 指图与原物一样大。

normal.en: Actually often means in reality, and in speech it can also soften a correction.
normal.cn: actually 常表示「其实」，口语里也能用来缓和一句纠正。

normal.en: Do not use actual where you mean current; actual is about fact, not about now.
normal.cn: 想说「当前的」不要用 actual；actual 讲的是事实，不是时间。

abstract.en: An estimate crossed out and a smaller, harder number written in.
abstract.cn: 一个估算被划掉，换上一个更小、更硬的数字。

abstract.en: A photograph next to a painted dream of the same street.
abstract.cn: 同一条街的照片，挨着一幅画出来的梦。

abstract.en: A receipt still warm from the printer, proving the thing was bought.
abstract.cn: 一张还带着打印机温度的收据，证明东西真的被买过。

examples.en: The actual cost of the repair was twice the estimate.
examples.cn: 修理的实际成本是估算的两倍。

examples.en: In actual fact, she had never left the country.
examples.cn: 事实上，她从未离开过这个国家。

examples.en: The actual size of the hall surprised the whole band.
examples.cn: 大厅的实际尺寸让整个乐队都吃了一惊。

root: 源自拉丁语 actualis「以行动形式存在的」，由 agere「做、驱动」的分词 actus 加形容词词尾 -alis 构成；经古法语 actuel 于十四世纪进入英语，先指真实行为与事实，后引申为与估算相对的确切数额。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses of one word: what really exists, and what is stated exactly instead of guessed.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个词的两个义项：真正存在的东西，以及不说约数而说准数的那个数字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an estimate replaced by the number that was actually paid.
core.cn: 核心意象：估算被换成真正付出去的那个数字。

branches.en: THE FACT: what exists can be pointed at, unlike a plan.
branches.cn: 事实线：存在的东西能被指认，计划不能。

branches.en: THE FIGURE: an exact number ends the guessing.
branches.cn: 数字线：确切数字终结了猜测。

branches.en: THE CONTRAST: actual always pushes against imagined or expected.
branches.cn: 对照线：actual 总是顶着「想象」或「预期」。

branches.en: THE LEDGER: a checked invoice makes a figure actual.
branches.cn: 账本线：核对过的发票让一个数字变成 actual。

branches.en: THE PHOTOGRAPH: the picture shows the actual street, not the map of it.
branches.cn: 照片线：照片给出真实的街道，而不是它的地图。

intro.en: The act- stem supplies the idea of done, and the adjective suffix -al turns it into a description of fact.
intro.cn: act- 词干提供「已做成」的意思，形容词后缀 -al 把它变成对事实的描述。

latinIntro.en: Latin actualis is attested, and French actuel carried it toward English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 actualis 有文献可证，法语 actuel 把它带到英语门前。

items.example: It keeps the idea of something done.
items.exampleCN: 它保留「已经做成」的意思。

items.example: It gives the stem act- to the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它把词干 act- 交给这个形容词。

items.example: It is the direct model of actual.
items.exampleCN: 它是 actual 的直接原型。

items.example: It forms actual from act.

items.example: It forms actually.

items.exampleCN: 它把 act 变成动词形式 acts。

definition_en: the state of being real; what is real as opposed to what is imagined or planned
core_image: 镜头对准一间普通厨房，锅里真的在冒热气
scene: 那位纪录片导演说，他不想要漂亮构图，只想让镜头拍到事情本来的样子。The documentary maker wanted no beautiful framing; he wanted the camera to catch actuality.
sceneCN: 这里 actuality 指未经修饰的真实状况（第 1 个义项：现实）；句意为导演不要漂亮构图，只想拍到事情本来的样子。

derivatives.zh: 由 act 加 -al 构成，义为「实际的；真实的」
由 actual 加 -ly 构成，义为「实际上；竟然」
由 actual 加 -ize 构成，义为「实现；使成为现实」

senses.title: Reality as opposed to imagination
senses.definition: the real state of things, especially when it differs from what was expected
senses.definitionCN: 事物的真实状况，尤指与预期不同的时候
senses.example: In actuality, the journey lasted three days.
senses.exampleCN: 实际上，这段旅程持续了三天。
senses.why: The noun names what has been done and exists, which is why it so often corrects a plan.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词命名的是已经做成、已经存在的东西，所以它常用来纠正计划。

senses.title: The quality of being real
senses.definition: the degree to which something feels or is genuinely real
senses.definitionCN: 某物在感受上或事实上真正真实的程度
senses.example: The recording gives the scene a strange actuality.
senses.exampleCN: 这段录音给这个场景带来一种奇特的真实感。
senses.why: Beyond the facts themselves, the noun also measures how strongly reality comes through.
senses.whyCN: 除了事实本身，这个名词还衡量现实穿透出来的强度。

intro.en: Actuality is the abstract noun of actual: the state of having been done and therefore being real.
intro.cn: actuality 是 actual 的抽象名词：已经被做成、因而真实存在的状态。

items.en: Agere meant to do, the verb at the root of the whole family.
items.cn: agere 意为「做」，是整个词族根部的动词。

items.en: Actus, a doing, gave the stem act- used by the nouns.
items.cn: actus 表示「一次做」，提供了名词所用的 act- 词干。

items.en: Actualis meant existing in act rather than merely in possibility.
items.cn: actualis 指以行动形式存在，而不只是停留在可能性里。

items.en: English formed the adjective first, and used it for real deeds and facts.
items.cn: 英语先造出形容词，用它指真实的行为与事实。

items.en: The suffix -ity then made actuality, the state or quality of being real.
items.cn: 随后后缀 -ity 造出 actuality，即「真实」这一状态或性质。

note.en: The look-alike group is the actual family; the near-meaning group is the nouns of reality.
note.cn: 形近组是 actual 词族；近义组是表示「现实」的名词。

entries.definition: Real and existing, not imagined.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「实际的；真实的」。

entries.definition: In fact; really.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「实际上；竟然」。

entries.definition: To do something or perform a role.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「行动；表演」。

entries.definition: The world as it really is.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「现实」，最通用。

entries.definition: Something known to be true.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「事实」，指可核实的一点。

entries.definition: What is the case, or the quality of being true.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「真相；真实性」。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep actuality close to the documentary camera and the corrected plan.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把 actuality 拴在纪录片镜头和被纠正的计划旁边。

normal.en: Actuality is actual plus -ity, so it names the state of being real.
normal.cn: actuality 是 actual 加 -ity，命名的是「真实」这一状态。

normal.en: In actuality is the phrase that opens a correction of what people assume.
normal.cn: in actuality 是用来纠正众人假设的那个开头。

normal.en: Radio producers call real recorded sound actuality, as opposed to studio talk.
normal.cn: 广播制作人把现场录下的真实声音称作 actuality，与棚内谈话相对。

normal.en: A scene gains actuality when the background noise is kept, not cleaned away.
normal.cn: 保留背景杂音而不清理掉，一个场景就获得了真实感。

normal.en: Do not confuse actuality with activity: one is reality, the other is doing things.
normal.cn: 别把 actuality 与 activity 混了：一个是现实，一个是活动。

abstract.en: A kitchen with steam on the window and no music added.
abstract.cn: 一间窗上有水汽、没有配乐的厨房。

abstract.en: A tape still carrying the cough of the person who recorded it.
abstract.cn: 一盘还留着录音者咳嗽声的磁带。

abstract.en: A plan lying beside the map that was actually walked.
abstract.cn: 一份计划，和真正走过的地图放在一起。

examples.en: In actuality, the meeting took less than ten minutes.
examples.cn: 实际上，那次会议不到十分钟。

examples.en: The film catches the actuality of a night shift in a hospital.
examples.cn: 这部影片捕捉到了医院夜班的真实状况。

examples.en: She doubted the actuality of everything he described.
examples.cn: 她怀疑他描述的一切是否真实存在。

root: 由英语 actual 加拉丁语抽象名词后缀 -ity 构成；actual 源自拉丁语 actualis「以行动形式存在的」，其根为 agere「做、驱动」的分词 actus；该词十七世纪定型，指真实存在的状态，也用于纪实录音与实况。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses: the real state of things, and the felt quality of being real.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项：事物真实的状况，以及「显得真实」的那种质感。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a camera pointed at an ordinary kitchen where something is really cooking.
core.cn: 核心意象：镜头对准一间普通厨房，锅里真的在冒热气。

branches.en: THE CORRECTION: actuality is what turns out to be the case.
branches.cn: 纠正线：actuality 是最后证实的那个情况。

branches.en: THE TEXTURE: realness can be felt, not only known.
branches.cn: 质感线：真实不只能被知道，也能被感觉到。

branches.en: THE RECORD: a tape keeps the hour as it was lived.
branches.cn: 记录线：磁带把那个小时按原样留住。

branches.en: THE ABSENCE OF POLISH: no music, no lighting gel, no retake.
branches.cn: 未修饰线：没有配乐、没有色纸、没有重来。

branches.en: THE DOCUMENT: a report of actuality lists what happened.
branches.cn: 文书线：一份 actuality 记录列出真正发生的事。

intro.en: The do-stem act- and two Latin suffixes -al and -ity build the word step by step.
intro.cn: 表示「做」的词干 act- 加上两个拉丁后缀 -al 与 -ity，一步步搭出这个词。

latinIntro.en: Actualis is attested in Latin, and the suffix -itas regularly became English -ity.
latinIntro.cn: actualis 在拉丁语中有文献可证，后缀 -itas 常规律地变为英语 -ity。

items.example: It carries the idea of something done.
items.exampleCN: 它承载「已经做成」的意思。

items.example: It supplies the stem act-.
items.exampleCN: 它提供词干 act-。

items.example: It is the base of the English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它是英语形容词的基础。

items.example: It forms actual.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 actual。

items.example: It forms actuality.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 actuality。

items.example: It forms actually.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 actually。

items.example: It forms actualize.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 actualize。

items.example: It forms actualities.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 actualities。

derivatives.zh: 由 act 加 -al 构成，义为「实际的；真实的」
由 actual 加 -ly 构成，义为「实际上；竟然」

definition_en: a medical practice of inserting thin needles at points on the body; the insertion of such needles
core_image: 几根细如发丝的银针稳稳立在皮肤上，病人的肩慢慢松下来
scene: 他长期伏案，肩颈硬得像块板，按摩几次都没用，最后去看了位老中医。After massage failed, he went to an old doctor who treated his stiff shoulder with acupuncture.
sceneCN: 这里 acupuncture 指用针刺穴位来治疗的方法（第 1 个义项：针灸疗法）；句意为按摩无效后，他去找一位老中医做针灸。

derivatives.zh: 由 acupuncture 加 -ist 构成，义为「针灸师」
由 acu- 加 point 构成，义为「穴位」

senses.title: The medical practice
senses.definition: a system of treatment that inserts needles at defined points to relieve pain or illness
senses.definitionCN: 在特定穴位上刺入针以缓解疼痛或治疗疾病的一套疗法
senses.example: Acupuncture is covered by some health insurance plans.
senses.exampleCN: 有些医疗保险涵盖针灸。
senses.why: The word names the whole practice, needles and points together, as one branch of medicine.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是整套医术，把针与穴位合在一起，作为医学的一个分支。

senses.title: The act of needling
senses.definition: the physical insertion of needles into those points during a session
senses.definitionCN: 在治疗过程中把针刺入那些穴位的具体操作
senses.example: The acupuncture itself took only twenty minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 针刺本身只用了二十分钟。
senses.why: The same noun can point at the hands-on act rather than the discipline, which is why it takes itself as subject.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词也能指手上那个具体动作，而不是那门学科，所以它可以直接做主语。

intro.en: Acupuncture is a Latin-built word: needle plus puncture, named in English for a practice far older than the name.
intro.cn: acupuncture 是用拉丁语部件造出的词：针加穿刺；这门医术比这个名字古老得多。

items.en: Acus meant a needle, and also the sharp point of anything.
items.cn: acus 意为「针」，也指任何东西的尖端。

items.en: Punctura meant a pricking or a puncture, from pungere, to prick.
items.cn: punctura 意为「刺、穿孔」，出自 pungere「刺」。

items.en: The two were joined into a learned Latin term for needling.
items.cn: 两者被组合成一个学术拉丁语词，指用针刺。

items.en: English physicians coined acupuncture while writing about Far Eastern medicine.
items.cn: 英国医生在介绍远东医学的文章里造出了 acupuncture。

items.en: The word widened to cover the whole practice, its points, its needles and its clinics.
items.cn: 这个词扩展为整套医术，包含穴位、针具与诊所。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the needle root; the near-meaning group is other hands-on therapies.
note.cn: 形近组共享「针」这个词根；近义组是其他以手法施治的疗法。

entries.definition: A person trained to practise acupuncture.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「针灸师」。

entries.definition: A point on the body used in acupuncture.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「穴位」。

entries.definition: A small hole made by something sharp.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小孔、穿刺」，与后半部分同源。

entries.definition: A therapy that burns dried herbs near the skin.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「艾灸」，常与针灸并用。

entries.definition: Rubbing and pressing the body to relieve tension.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「按摩」，同为手法治疗。

entries.definition: Treatment by movement and physical means.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「物理治疗」。

normalIntro.en: The hooks split the word into needle and puncture, then put the needle back into the clinic.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把词拆成「针」与「穿刺」，再把针放回诊所里。

normal.en: Acu- means needle, so acupuncture is literally needling.
normal.cn: acu- 意为「针」，所以 acupuncture 字面上就是「用针刺」。

normal.en: The second half is the same as puncture, a small hole pricked into something.
normal.cn: 后半部分与 puncture 相同，指被刺出的小孔。

normal.en: Chinese practice is far older than the English name, which was coined in the seventeenth century.
normal.cn: 中国这门医术远比英语名字古老，后者是十七世纪才造的。

normal.en: An acupuncturist works at acupoints with fine needles, often leaving them in for twenty minutes.
normal.cn: 针灸师在穴位上用细针，常留针二十分钟。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with moxibustion, which burns herbs rather than inserting needles.
normal.cn: 别与 moxibustion 混了，后者烧的是艾草，不是把针扎进去。

abstract.en: Silver threads standing in skin like tiny masts.
abstract.cn: 银线立在皮肤上，像一根根小桅杆。

abstract.en: A shoulder that has been hard for years quietly letting go.
abstract.cn: 一只硬了许多年的肩膀，悄悄松了下来。

abstract.en: A hand that knows exactly where to place the next needle.
abstract.cn: 一只清楚下一针该落在哪里的手。

examples.en: Acupuncture helped her sleep through the pain.
examples.cn: 针灸帮她熬过了疼痛，能睡个整觉。

examples.en: He tried acupuncture after the pills stopped working.
examples.cn: 药片失效之后，他尝试了针灸。

examples.en: The clinic offers acupuncture alongside herbal medicine.
examples.cn: 这家诊所把针灸与草药并用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿Q 帮克车」——阿Q 帮人把针克在车上，一路扎到穴位

root: 由拉丁语 acus「针」与 punctura「穿刺」（出自 pungere「刺」）合成，十七世纪英语医生在介绍远东医学时造出该词；最初指针刺这一操作，后扩展为包括穴位、针具与临床的整套疗法。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses: the whole branch of medicine, and the particular act of inserting the needles.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项：作为一门医术的针灸，以及把针真正扎进去的那一次操作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: fine needles standing still on the skin while a tight shoulder loosens.
core.cn: 核心意象：细针稳稳立在皮肤上，紧绷的肩膀慢慢松开。

branches.en: THE INSERTION: the needle goes in at a chosen point.
branches.cn: 进针线：针在选定的穴位上刺入。

branches.en: THE SENSATION: a dull ache tells the point has been reached.
branches.cn: 针感线：一种沉沉的酸胀说明扎到了位置。

branches.en: THE CLINIC: the practice gathers points, needles and training.
branches.cn: 诊所线：这套医术把穴位、针具与训练聚在一起。

branches.en: THE COURSE: treatment is repeated over weeks.
branches.cn: 疗程线：治疗要按周重复。

branches.en: THE INSURANCE: some plans pay for it as ordinary care.
branches.cn: 保险线：有些保险把它当作常规医疗来支付。

intro.en: A Latin word for needle and a Latin word for pricking were welded into one English term.
intro.cn: 一个意为「针」的拉丁词与一个意为「穿刺」的拉丁词，被焊接成一个英语术语。

latinIntro.en: Acus and punctura are both attested in Latin; the compound is a learned English coinage.
latinIntro.cn: acus 与 punctura 在拉丁语中均有文献可证；这个复合词是英语的学术造词。

items.example: It supplies the needle at the front of the word.
items.exampleCN: 它提供这个词开头的「针」。

items.example: It is the source of the first element.
items.exampleCN: 它是第一个构词成分的来源。

items.example: It gives the second half of the word.
items.exampleCN: 它提供这个词的后半部分。

items.example: It is the verb behind punctura.
items.exampleCN: 它是 punctura 背后的动词。

items.example: It appears in puncture and in the second half of acupuncture.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 puncture 以及 acupuncture 的后半部分。

items.example: It forms acupuncturist.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 acupuncturist。

items.example: It keeps the pricking sense visible.
items.exampleCN: 它让「被刺」这层意思仍然可见。

items.example: It shortens acu- and joins it to point.
items.exampleCN: 它把 acu- 缩短后与 point 连在一起。

derivatives.zh: 由 acupuncture 加 -ist 构成，义为「针灸师」
由 acu- 加 point 构成，义为「穴位」

definition_zh: 敏锐的；急性的；严重的；尖的
definition_en: sharp in perception; of an illness, sudden and severe; of a problem, very serious; of an angle, less than ninety degrees
core_image: 一枚磨得极尖的针，轻轻一碰就有反应
scene: 电话那头只停顿了半秒，他就听出对方在犹豫。Over the phone he caught the faintest hesitation, so acute was his ear.
sceneCN: 这里 acute 指感官极其敏锐（第 1 个义项：敏锐的）；句意为电话那头的半秒停顿也逃不过他的耳朵。

pos.zh: 敏锐的；急性的；严重的；尖的

derivatives.zh: 由 acute 加 -ly 构成，义为「敏锐地；强烈地」
由 acute 加 -ness 构成，义为「敏锐；尖锐」
与 acute 同根，义为「（感官的）敏锐度」

senses.title: Sharp in perception
senses.definition: able to notice small details with the senses or the mind
senses.definitionCN: 感官或心思能察觉到细小差别的
senses.example: Her acute hearing caught the click of the lock.
senses.exampleCN: 她敏锐的耳朵捕捉到了锁扣的响声。
senses.why: The Latin adjective means sharpened, so an acute mind or ear cuts through noise.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁形容词意为「被磨尖的」，所以敏锐的心思或耳朵能切开噪音。

senses.title: Sudden and severe, of illness
senses.definition: of a disease, starting suddenly and sharply rather than lasting long
senses.definitionCN: 指疾病突然而猛烈地发作，而非长期持续
senses.example: He was admitted with acute pain in his chest.
senses.exampleCN: 他因胸部剧痛被收治入院。
senses.why: A sharp point describes an illness that strikes at once, cutting through the body's calm.
senses.whyCN: 尖锐的尖端形容来势迅猛的病，一下子划破身体的平静。

senses.title: Very serious, of a problem
senses.definition: of a difficulty or need, extreme and urgent
senses.definitionCN: 指困难或需求达到极端而紧迫的程度
senses.example: The city faces an acute shortage of nurses.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市面临护士的严重短缺。
senses.why: A shortage that is acute has reached a point sharp enough to hurt every day.
senses.whyCN: 短缺到了 acute 的程度，就是尖锐到每天都在伤人。

senses.title: Of an angle below ninety degrees
senses.definition: of an angle, measuring less than a right angle
senses.definitionCN: 指角度小于直角的
senses.example: The roof meets the wall at an acute angle.
senses.exampleCN: 屋顶与墙面形成一个锐角。
senses.why: This is the oldest literal sense: the shape that is physically pointed.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的字面义：形状上真的是尖的。

intro.en: Acute comes from a Latin verb meaning to sharpen, and the sharp point explains every later sense.
intro.cn: acute 出自一个意为「磨尖」的拉丁动词，那个尖点解释了后来所有义项。

items.en: Acus meant a needle, the model of everything sharp.
items.cn: acus 意为「针」，是一切尖锐之物的原型。

items.en: Acuere meant to sharpen or to whet, and gave the adjective its idea.
items.cn: acuere 意为「磨尖、磨利」，为这个形容词提供了核心意思。

items.en: Acutus described what has been sharpened, from a needle to a wit.
items.cn: acutus 形容被磨尖的东西，从针尖到机锋。

items.en: English borrowed it for sharp senses and for sharp angles.
items.cn: 英语借来它，用于敏锐的感官与尖锐的角度。

items.en: Medicine made acute the partner of chronic: sharp and short against slow and long.
items.cn: 医学让 acute 与 chronic 成对：尖锐而短暂，对缓慢而漫长。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the sharpen root; the near-meaning group is the adjectives of sharpness and severity.
note.cn: 形近组共享「磨尖」词根；近义组是表示尖锐与严重的形容词。

entries.definition: Sharpness of sight, hearing or mind.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「敏锐度」，多用于感官。

entries.definition: The quality of being acute.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「敏锐；尖锐」。

entries.definition: Quickness and sharpness of judgment.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「精明、敏锐的判断力」。

entries.definition: Having a fine edge; quick to notice.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「锋利的；敏锐的」，最通用。

entries.definition: Very sensitive or eager.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「敏锐的；热切的」。

entries.definition: Very bad or serious.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「严重的」，只用于程度。

entries.definition: At a point of serious danger or decision.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「危急的；关键的」。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the needle in view: sharp senses, sharp illness, sharp shortage, sharp angle.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子始终把那根针留在眼前：尖锐的感官、尖锐的病、尖锐的短缺、尖锐的角。

normal.en: Acu- means needle, so acute is the adjective of a sharpened point.
normal.cn: acu- 意为「针」，所以 acute 就是「被磨尖的尖端」那个形容词。

normal.en: An acute illness is short and sharp; a chronic one is long and dull.
normal.cn: acute 的病短而尖，chronic 的病长而钝。

normal.en: An acute angle is the sharp one, smaller than a right angle.
normal.cn: acute angle 是那个尖的角，比直角小。

normal.en: Acute hearing hears what others miss; acute judgment sees what others overlook.
normal.cn: 敏锐的耳朵听见别人漏掉的，敏锐的判断看见别人忽略的。

normal.en: In hospital notes, acute often means it started today, not that it is fatal.
normal.cn: 在病历里，acute 常指「今天突然发作」，并不等于致命。

abstract.en: A needle so fine it finds the one tight nerve in a whole shoulder.
abstract.cn: 一根细到能在一整只肩膀里找到那根紧绷神经的针。

abstract.en: A pain that arrives like a door slammed shut.
abstract.cn: 像门被砰地关上那样到来的疼痛。

abstract.en: A corner of a roof sharp enough to cut the sky.
abstract.cn: 一个尖得能划破天空的屋角。

examples.en: Her acute hearing caught the click of the lock.
examples.cn: 她敏锐的耳朵捕捉到了锁扣的响声。

examples.en: The city faces an acute shortage of nurses.
examples.cn: 这座城市面临护士的严重短缺。

examples.en: He was taken to hospital with acute pain in his chest.
examples.cn: 他因胸部剧痛被送进医院。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额Q特」——额头上扎一针，Q 特敏感，一点动静就知道

root: 源自拉丁语 acutus「被磨尖的」，出自 acuere「磨尖、磨利」，其根为 acus「针」；十四世纪进入英语，先指尖锐的角度与敏锐的感官，现代医学又用它表示「急性」，与 chronic 相对。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of one sharp point: a keen sense, a sudden illness, an urgent shortage, and a narrow angle.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个尖点的四个义项：敏锐的感官、突然发作的病、紧迫的短缺，以及一个窄角。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a needle sharpened until the least touch registers.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根被磨到极致的针，最轻的一触都能感到。

branches.en: THE EAR: sharpness becomes the ability to notice.
branches.cn: 耳朵线：尖锐变成了察觉力。

branches.en: THE BODY: a disease strikes suddenly, like a point.
branches.cn: 身体线：疾病像尖端一样突然袭来。

branches.en: THE SHORTAGE: a need becomes sharp enough to hurt.
branches.cn: 短缺线：需求尖锐到开始伤人。

branches.en: THE ANGLE: the literal shape that is truly pointed.
branches.cn: 角线：字面意义上真正尖的那个形状。

branches.en: THE MIND: acute judgment cuts to the real issue.
branches.cn: 头脑线：敏锐的判断直接切到真正的问题。

intro.en: A Latin word for needle, a verb for sharpening and an adjective ending built acute.
intro.cn: 一个意为「针」的拉丁词、一个表示「磨尖」的动词、一个形容词词尾，造出了 acute。

latinIntro.en: Acus, acuere and acutus are all attested; English records acute from the fourteenth century.
latinIntro.cn: acus、acuere、acutus 均有文献可证；英语自十四世纪起记录 acute。

items.example: It carries the sharp point inside the word.
items.exampleCN: 它把那个尖端带进词里。

items.example: It is the root noun of the family.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个词族的名词根。

items.example: It supplies the action behind acute.
items.exampleCN: 它提供 acute 背后的那个动作。

items.example: It is the direct model of acute.
items.exampleCN: 它是 acute 的直接原型。

items.example: It keeps the Latin shape of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它保留了形容词的拉丁语外形。

items.example: It forms acutely.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 acutely。

items.example: It forms acuteness.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 acuteness。

items.example: It forms acuity from the same root.
items.exampleCN: 它用同一个词根构成 acuity。

由 acute 加 -ness 构成，义为「敏锐；尖锐」

definition_en: to change oneself to fit new conditions; to change something so that it fits a new use; to rewrite a work for another medium
core_image: 一件旧家具被改了几处，恰好卡进新房间的墙角
scene: 搬进老房子后，他们把门框削宽，把搁板放低，好让轮椅顺利通过。After moving into the old house they adapted the doorway and the shelves so that the wheelchair could pass.
sceneCN: 这里 adapted 指改动物件使其适合新用途（第 3 个义项：改装）；句意为他们改宽门框、放低搁板，让轮椅能通过。

collocations.phrase: adapt a novel for the screen

derivatives.zh: 由 adapt 加 -ation 构成，义为「适应；改编本」
由 adapt 加 -able 构成，义为「能适应的；可改装的」
由 adapt 加 -er 构成，义为「适配器；转接器」

senses.title: To fit into new conditions
senses.definition: to change one's behaviour so as to live or work well in a new situation
senses.definitionCN: 改变自身行为，以便在新环境中生活或工作得好
senses.example: Children adapt to a new language faster than adults do.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子适应一门新语言比大人快。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to fit to, so adapting is making oneself fit the new frame.
senses.whyCN: 那个拉丁动词意为「使适合」，所以适应就是把自己嵌进新的框子。

senses.title: To rewrite a work for another medium
senses.definition: to change a book, play or story into a form suitable for film, stage or another use
senses.definitionCN: 把书、剧本或故事改写为适合影视、舞台或其他用途的形式
senses.example: The studio adapted the novel into a six-part series.
senses.exampleCN: 制片方把这部小说改编成了六集剧。
senses.why: A story must be cut to fit a new running time and a new set of eyes.
senses.whyCN: 一个故事必须被剪裁，才能塞进新的时长和新的观看方式。

senses.title: To alter an object for a new use
senses.definition: to modify a device or space so that it serves a different purpose
senses.definitionCN: 改动一件器具或空间，使其服务于另一种用途
senses.example: They adapted the old barn into a workshop.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把那座旧谷仓改成了工作坊。
senses.why: The object keeps its bones but is fitted to a job it was not made for.
senses.whyCN: 物件保留原来的骨架，却被装进一件它原本不是为此而做的活。

intro.en: Adapt comes from a Latin verb meaning to fit to, and every sense is a kind of fitting.
intro.cn: adapt 出自一个意为「使适合」的拉丁动词，每个义项都是一种「装到合适」。

items.en: Aptus meant fitted, suitable, well joined to something.
items.cn: aptus 意为「合适的、接得恰到好处的」。

items.en: Aptare meant to fit or fasten one thing to another.
items.cn: aptare 意为「把一物装到另一物上」。

items.en: The prefix ad-, to, made adaptare: to fit something toward a purpose.
items.cn: 前缀 ad-「向」造出 adaptare，即「朝某个用途去装fit」。

items.en: French used the verb for fitting and for making suitable.
items.cn: 法语用这个动词表示「装配合适」。

items.en: English took it up, and the literary sense of rewriting grew in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 英语采纳了它，改写作品的文学义在十八世纪成长起来。

note.en: The look-alike pair adopt and adapt is a classic trap; the near-meaning group is the verbs of fitting.
note.cn: 形近组里的 adopt 与 adapt 是经典陷阱；近义组是表示「使合适」的动词。

entries.definition: To take a child as one's own, or to take up an idea.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「收养；采纳」，与 adapt 只差一个字母。

entries.definition: The act of fitting, or a rewritten work.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「适应；改编本」。

entries.definition: Able to change to fit new conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「能适应的」。

entries.definition: To change slightly so as to fit or work better.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「调整」，改动幅度通常较小。

entries.definition: To make room for or suit the needs of.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「容纳；迁就」。

entries.definition: To change something in part.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「修改」，强调部分改动。

entries.definition: To write something again in a new form.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「重写」，对应改编义。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the idea of fitting: a person to a place, a story to a screen, an object to a new job.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子都守住「装到合适」：人装进地方，故事装进屏幕，物件装进新用途。

normal.en: Adapt contains apt, meaning fitting, so it is about making a fit.
normal.cn: adapt 里藏着 apt「合适」，所以它讲的是把东西弄合适。

normal.en: Adapt to is for people and animals; adapt something is for objects and texts.
normal.cn: adapt to 用于人与动物；adapt something 用于物件与文本。

normal.en: A film adaptation cuts a book down to two hours.
normal.cn: 影视改编把一本书剪成两小时。

normal.en: An adapter is a small plug that makes one shape fit another.
normal.cn: adapter 是一个小插头，让一种形状接上另一种。

normal.en: Do not say adopt when you mean adapt: adopting takes something in, adapting changes it to fit.
normal.cn: 想说适应时别用 adopt：adopt 是收进来，adapt 是改到合适。

abstract.cn: 一张旧桌被锯短一条腿，在斜地板上重新站平。

abstract.en: A plant bending its leaves toward a window it did not choose.
abstract.cn: 一株植物把叶子弯向一扇它并未选择的窗。

abstract.en: A story cut and resewn until it fits a new body.
abstract.cn: 一个故事被剪开重缝，直到合上新的身体。

examples.en: Children adapt to a new language faster than adults do.
examples.cn: 孩子适应一门新语言比大人快。

examples.en: The studio adapted the novel into a six-part series.
examples.cn: 制片方把这部小说改编成了六集剧。

root: 源自拉丁语 adaptare「使适合」，由 ad-「向」加 aptare「装配、使合适」构成，其根 aptus 意为「合适的」；经法语 adapter 于十七世纪进入英语，十八世纪发展出文学上的「改编」义。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses all describe making a fit: a person to a place, a story to a medium, an object to a new job.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项都在讲「弄到合适」：人适合地方，故事适合媒介，物件适合新用途。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something old altered just enough to sit perfectly in a new corner.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件旧物被改动几处，恰好卡进新的墙角。

branches.en: THE PERSON: behaviour changes until the place accepts it.
branches.cn: 人物线：行为改到被新地方接受为止。

branches.en: THE STORY: a text is cut to fit a new running time.
branches.cn: 故事线：文本被剪到新的时长里。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: an old frame is fitted to an unplanned job.
branches.cn: 物件线：旧骨架被装进一件没计划过的活。

branches.en: THE ANIMAL: a body adjusts its habits to a new climate.
branches.cn: 动物线：身体把习性调到新气候。

branches.en: THE ADAPTER: a small part that makes two shapes meet.
branches.cn: 转接线：一个小零件让两种形状接上。

intro.en: The prefix ad- points toward something, and the root apt- carries the idea of being fit.
intro.cn: 前缀 ad- 指向某处，词根 apt- 承载「合适」的意思。

latinIntro.en: Aptus, aptare and adaptare are attested in Latin; French adapter carried the verb to English.
latinIntro.cn: aptus、aptare、adaptare 在拉丁语中均有文献可证；法语 adapter 把这个动词带到英语。

items.example: It is the root idea behind adapt.

items.exampleCN: 它构成 adaptation。

由 adapt 加 -able 构成，义为「能适应的；可改装的」

definition_zh: 添加；把…加进去；相加；补充说
definition_en: to put something together with something else so that the amount grows; to join numbers into a total; to say something further
core_image: 一只手把最后一块积木轻轻放到已经搭好的塔顶
scene: 汤尝起来淡了点，她拧开盐罐，又往锅里撒了一小撮。She tasted the soup, found it flat, and added a pinch of salt to the pot.
sceneCN: 这里 add 指把盐加进汤里（第 1 个义项：添加、加入）；句意为她觉得汤淡，又往锅里加了一小撮盐。

senses.title: Put in as well
senses.definition: to put something into or onto something else so that it becomes part of it
senses.definitionCN: 把某物放进或放到另一物上，使它成为其中一部分
senses.example: Add the garlic once the oil is hot.
senses.exampleCN: 油热后加入大蒜。
senses.why: This is the physical core of the word: one more thing is placed beside what is already there.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词的物理核心：又一样东西被放到已有的东西旁边。

senses.title: Join numbers
senses.definition: to combine two or more numbers or amounts so as to obtain a total
senses.definitionCN: 把两个或更多的数字或数量合并，得出总数
senses.example: If you add seven and five, you get twelve.
senses.exampleCN: 七加五等于十二。
senses.why: Arithmetic treats the same joining gesture as an operation, and the result is called a sum.
senses.whyCN: 算术把同一个「并到一起」的动作当成一次运算，结果叫作和。

senses.title: Say further
senses.definition: to say something more, often to explain or strengthen what has just been said
senses.definitionCN: 再说什么，常用来解释或加强刚刚说过的话
senses.example: She added that the office would close early.
senses.exampleCN: 她补充说办公室会提前关门。
senses.why: Speech borrows the old image again: one more remark is laid on top of the first.
senses.whyCN: 说话又一次借用了这个旧意象：再一句话被放到第一句上面。

intro.en: add is Latin addere worn down to its bare stem, and every modern sense still carries the old gesture of giving one thing to another.
intro.cn: add 是拉丁语 addere 磨去词尾后留下的词干，今天每一个义项都还带着「把一样东西给到另一样东西」的老动作。

items.en: Addere meant to give to or put to, formed from ad- and dare.
items.cn: addere 意为「给到、放到」，由 ad- 与 dare 构成。

items.en: The prefix pointed the action towards something already present.
items.cn: 这个前缀把动作指向已经存在的某物。

items.en: Dare meant to give or to place, and it survives in English mainly inside compounds.
items.cn: dare 意为「给、放置」，在英语里主要残存在复合词中。

items.en: English borrowed the Latin verb early and shortened it to the bare form add.
items.cn: 英语很早借入这个拉丁动词，并把它缩短成 bare 形式的 add。

items.en: The counting sense grew beside the everyday one, and the reporting sense followed in speech.
items.cn: 计数的义项在日常义项旁成长起来，补充陈述的义项随后在口语中出现。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin root; the near-meaning group is other verbs of putting one thing with another.
note.cn: 形近组共享这个拉丁词根；近义组是其他表示「把一样东西与另一样放在一起」的动词。

entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「附录、补遗」。

entries.definition: The act of adding, or the thing added.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「添加；添加物；加法」。

entries.definition: A substance added in small amounts for a purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「添加剂」。

entries.definition: To put something inside something else.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「插入」，强调放进内部。

entries.definition: To make someone or something part of a larger group.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「包括、纳入」。

entries.definition: To add something at the end of a piece of writing.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「附加、增补」，专指加在末尾。

normalIntro.en: The hooks split the word into its Latin parts, then walk through its three everyday uses.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把词拆成拉丁部件，再依次走过它的三个日常用法。

normal.en: add is Latin addere worn down: ad- means to, and dare means give.
normal.cn: add 是磨短了的拉丁语 addere：ad- 意为「向」，dare 意为「给」。

normal.en: Every sense keeps the same picture, one thing placed with another.
normal.cn: 每个义项都保留同一幅画：一样东西被放到另一样旁边。

normal.en: Numbers are only the clearest case, since seven and five visibly make twelve.
normal.cn: 数字只是最清楚的例子，因为七和五看得见地凑成十二。

normal.en: A remark is added when the first sentence still feels incomplete.
normal.cn: 第一句还显得不完整时，就会再补一句。

normal.en: The phrase add up means both to total and, informally, to make sense.
normal.cn: 短语 add up 既指「加起来」，口语里也指「说得通」。

abstract.cn: 一小撮盐消失在蒸汽里。

abstract.en: A ledger line growing by one more figure.
abstract.cn: 账本上的一行又多出一个数字。

abstract.en: A sentence that continues after a short pause.
abstract.cn: 一句话在短暂停顿之后继续下去。

examples.cn: 如果酱汁变稠，就加一点水。

examples.en: He added two columns of figures in his head.
examples.cn: 他在心里把两列数字加了起来。

examples.en: The teacher added a note in the margin.
examples.cn: 老师在页边补了一条批注。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱得」——爱得深就总想再多给一点，于是不断往里面加

root: 源自拉丁语 addere「给到、加到」，由 ad-「向」与 dare「给」合成；英语早期借入后缩为 add，先指把东西放到一起，后发展出算术相加与补充说话两个义项。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: putting something in, joining numbers, and saying one more thing.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：把东西加进去、把数字相加、再补充一句话。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a last pinch of salt falling into a simmering pot.
core.cn: 核心意象：最后一小撮盐落进正在咕嘟的锅里。

branches.en: THE PINCH: a small amount goes into what is already cooking.
branches.cn: 调味线：一小撮东西进入已经在煮的食物。

branches.en: THE PILE: each new item sits beside the ones already there.
branches.cn: 堆叠线：每一件新东西都挨着原有的那些。

branches.en: THE SUM: numbers are joined until a single total remains.
branches.cn: 求和线：数字被并到一起，最后只剩一个总数。

branches.en: THE REMARK: one more sentence is laid on the conversation.
branches.cn: 补充线：又一句话被放到对话上面。

branches.en: THE LARGER WHOLE: what results is more than what was there before.
branches.cn: 整体线：得到的结果比原先的更多。

definition_en: a person who cannot stop using a drug or repeating a habit; to make someone dependent on a substance or activity
core_image: 一个人反复回到同一盏灯下，手指已经不听使唤
scene: 他起初只是每晚喝一瓶，后来不喝就睡不着，家人才意识到他已经成瘾。He began with one bottle a night, then could not sleep without it, and his family realized he had become an addict.
sceneCN: 这里 addict 指被某种习惯或药物控制住的人（第 1 个义项：成瘾者）；句意为他从每晚一瓶到离不开酒，家人这才看出他已成瘾。

senses.title: The person held by a habit
senses.definition: a person who is unable to stop taking a drug or repeating a habit even when it harms them
senses.definitionCN: 无法停止使用某种药物或重复某种习惯、即使受到伤害的人
senses.example: The clinic treats addicts from every walk of life.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所接待各行各业的成瘾者。
senses.why: The noun points at the person, while the substance or habit stays in the background as the thing that holds them.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指的是人，药物或习惯则留在背景里，是控制住他们的那个东西。

senses.title: To make someone dependent
senses.definition: to cause a person to become dependent on a substance or activity
senses.definitionCN: 使某人对某种物质或活动产生依赖
senses.example: Strong painkillers can addict a patient within weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 强效止痛药可能在几周内就让病人成瘾。
senses.why: The verb turns the condition into an action, with the drug or habit as the doer.
senses.whyCN: 动词把这个状态变成一次动作，药物或习惯成了施行者。

intro.en: addict began as a legal word for a person handed over to another, and only later named a person handed over to a habit.
intro.cn: addict 最初是个法律用语，指被交付给他人的人；后来才指被交给某种习惯的人。

items.en: Addicere meant to assign or surrender a person or thing to another.
items.cn: addicere 意为把某人或某物判归、交付给另一方。

items.en: The past participle addictus described someone legally bound over.
items.cn: 过去分词 addictus 指在法律上被交出去的人。

items.en: An addictus was a debtor assigned to work for a creditor until the debt was settled.
items.cn: 在罗马法里，addictus 是判给债主干活抵债的欠债人。

items.en: English took the word for a person given over to a practice or a passion.
items.cn: 英语借来这个词，指把自己交给某种做法或激情的人。

items.en: The sense narrowed towards drugs and compulsive habits, and a verb grew beside the noun.
items.cn: 词义逐渐收窄到药物与强迫性习惯，名词旁边又长出一个动词。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the addiction root; the near-meaning group is other words for people caught by a substance.
note.cn: 形近组共享「成瘾」这个词根；近义组是其他表示被某种物质抓住的人的词。

entries.definition: The condition of being unable to stop using something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成瘾；瘾」。

entries.definition: Causing a person to become dependent.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「使人上瘾的」。

entries.definition: Unable to stop using a substance or habit.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「上瘾的、沉迷的」。

entries.definition: A person who takes a drug, especially one who does so regularly.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「使用者」，常指经常吸毒的人。

entries.definition: A person who uses something harmful to excess.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「滥用者」。

entries.definition: A person who relies on a substance or on another person.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「依赖者」，可指依赖药物的人。

normalIntro.en: The hooks follow the word from a Roman courtroom to a modern clinic.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子跟着这个词从罗马法庭一路走到现代诊所。

normal.en: addict is Latin addictus, a person legally handed over to someone else.
normal.cn: addict 来自拉丁语 addictus，指在法律上被交给别人的人。

normal.en: The old image is a debtor bound to a creditor; the new one is a mind bound to a habit.
normal.cn: 旧的意象是欠债人被绑给债主；新的意象是心智被绑给习惯。

normal.en: The noun names the person, the verb names what the drug does to them.
normal.cn: 名词指人，动词指药物对他们所做的事。

normal.en: Addiction is the state, addictive is the pull, and addicted is the person under it.
normal.cn: addiction 是状态，addictive 是那股拉力，addicted 是被拉住的这个人。

normal.en: The word now covers gambling, screens and drink as easily as opium.
normal.cn: 今天这个词既能指鸦片，也能指赌博、屏幕和酒。

abstract.en: A hand reaching for a bottle before the mind agrees.
abstract.cn: 手先伸向瓶子，脑子还没同意。

abstract.en: A lamp left on for someone who keeps returning.
abstract.cn: 一盏为反复回来的人留着的灯。

abstract.en: A door that opens inwards and will not stay shut.
abstract.cn: 一扇只能往里开、关不上的门。

examples.en: He was an addict long before anyone noticed.
examples.cn: 在别人察觉之前很久，他就已经成瘾了。

examples.en: The drug can addict patients who take it for too long.
examples.cn: 这种药会让服用过久的病人成瘾。

examples.en: Addicts often hide the habit from those closest to them.
examples.cn: 成瘾者常常对最亲近的人隐瞒这个习惯。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱迪克特」——爱迪克特爱到无法脱身，就成了被习惯抓住的人

root: 源自拉丁语 addicere「判归、交付」的过去分词 addictus；在罗马法里指判给债主抵债的人，十七世纪英语借来指「把自己交给某种做法或激情的人」，现代又收窄到药物与强迫性习惯。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses, one for the person held by a habit and one for the force that holds them.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项：一个指被习惯抓住的人，一个指抓住他们的那股力量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaching for the same bottle without asking the mind.
core.cn: 核心意象：手已经伸向同一个瓶子，脑子还没发话。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the noun points at whoever is held.
branches.cn: 人物线：名词指向被控制住的那个人。

branches.en: THE SECRET: addicts often hide the habit from family.
branches.cn: 隐瞒线：成瘾者常对家人隐瞒这个习惯。

branches.en: THE DRUG: the verb points at what creates the dependence.
branches.cn: 药物线：动词指向造成依赖的那个东西。

branches.en: THE SPEED: dependence can form within a few weeks.
branches.cn: 速度线：依赖可能在几周内形成。

branches.en: THE LOOP: desire, use and return repeat without a clear end.
branches.cn: 循环线：欲望、使用与回归不断重复，没有明确的终点。

intro.en: addict comes from a Latin verb of assigning, built from ad- and dicere, and English later added the noun and verb endings around it.
intro.cn: addict 出自一个表示「判归」的拉丁动词，由 ad- 与 dicere 构成，英语后来在它周围加上名词与动词的词尾。

latinIntro.en: ad-, dicere and the participle addictus are all attested; the English forms are later shortenings.
latinIntro.cn: ad-、dicere 与分词 addictus 都有文献可证；英语形式是后来的缩短。

items.example: It directs the assigning towards another person.
items.exampleCN: 它把「判归」这个动作指向另一个人。

items.example: It supplies the declaring half of addicere.
items.exampleCN: 它提供 addicere 中「宣布」的那一半。

items.example: It is the form English borrowed first.
items.exampleCN: 它是英语最先借用的形式。

items.example: It turns addict into addiction.
items.exampleCN: 它把 addict 变成 addiction。

items.example: It forms addictive from the same stem.
items.exampleCN: 它用同一个词干构成 addictive。

items.example: It produces addicted.
items.exampleCN: 它产出 addicted。

items.example: It marks addicts in both noun and verb use.
items.exampleCN: 它既能标名词复数，也能标动词第三人称。

items.meaning: one given over to a habit
items.example: English shortened the Latin participle into this bare form.
items.exampleCN: 英语把拉丁分词缩短成这个光秃秃的形式。

derivatives.zh: 由 addict 加 -ion 构成，义为「成瘾；瘾」
由 addict 加 -ive 构成，义为「使人上瘾的」
由 addict 加 -ed 构成，义为「上瘾的、沉迷的」

definition_zh: 使人上瘾的；令人着迷的
definition_en: causing a person to become dependent on a substance or activity; so engaging that people want more and more
core_image: 一局结束，手指已经自动点了「再来一局」
scene: 那款小游戏规则简单，赢一把就想再赢一把，不少人说它格外让人上瘾。The little game had simple rules, and one win made players want another; many called it unusually addictive.
sceneCN: 这里 addictive 指让人上瘾、停不下来（第 1 个义项：使人上瘾的）；句意为一赢就想再赢，玩家觉得它特别容易让人沉迷。

pos.zh: 使人上瘾的；令人着迷的

derivatives.zh: 由 addictive 加 -ly 构成，义为「让人上瘾地」
由 addictive 加 -ness 构成，义为「成瘾性」
由同一词干构成，义为「成瘾者」
由 addict 加 -ion 构成，义为「成瘾」

senses.title: Causing real dependence
senses.definition: causing the body or mind to need a substance or activity more and more
senses.definitionCN: 使身体或心理对某种物质或活动越来越离不开
senses.example: Nicotine is one of the most addictive substances known.
senses.exampleCN: 尼古丁是已知最容易让人上瘾的物质之一。
senses.why: The adjective describes the power a thing has over the person who uses it, not the person's own weakness.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词描述的是某物对使用者施加的力量，而不是使用者本人的软弱。

senses.title: Hard to stop for pleasure alone
senses.definition: so engaging that people find it hard to stop, even when there is no physical dependence
senses.definitionCN: 极其吸引人，即使没有生理依赖也让人难以停下
senses.example: The show is addictive in the way a good puzzle is.
senses.exampleCN: 这部剧像一道好谜题那样让人停不下来。
senses.why: The same word stretches from drugs to pleasure, because the pull feels similar from the inside.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词从药物延伸到娱乐，因为从内心感受来说，那股拉力很像。

intro.en: addictive is a young adjective built on an old legal word; the ending -ive turned the act of handing someone over into a quality of the thing that does it.
intro.cn: addictive 是个年轻的形容词，长在一个古老的法律词上；词尾 -ive 把「把人交出去」的动作变成施事物的一种性质。

items.en: Addicere meant to assign, and its participle described a person handed over.
items.cn: addicere 意为判归，其分词描述被交付出去的人。

items.en: Addictus named the person bound over, not the thing that bound them.
items.cn: addictus 指被绑过去的人，而不是绑住他们的东西。

items.en: English used addict for someone given over to a practice or passion.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语用 addict 指把自己交给某种做法或激情的人。

items.en: Medical writing began to speak of drugs that create dependence.
items.cn: 医学写作开始谈论会制造依赖的药物。

items.en: The adjective widened again, so games and shows could be called addictive.
items.cn: 这个形容词再次扩展，游戏和节目也能被称作 addictive。

note.en: The look-alike group is the same family at different distances; the near-meaning group is other adjectives of strong pull.
note.cn: 形近组是同一家族在不同距离上的成员；近义组是其他表示「强拉力」的形容词。

entries.definition: Unable to stop using a substance or habit.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「上瘾的」，说的是人。

entries.definition: The state of being unable to stop.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成瘾」，说的是状态。

entries.definition: A person held by a habit.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成瘾者」，说的是人。

entries.definition: Tending to create a habit that is hard to break.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「容易成瘾的」，语气较中性。

entries.definition: So interesting that attention cannot easily leave it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「引人入胜的」，只指吸引力。

entries.definition: Pleasant and interesting enough to hold attention.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「迷人的、有趣的」，不含成瘾义。

normalIntro.en: The hooks separate the medical sense from the everyday sense of a pleasure that will not let go.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把医学上的成瘾与日常里「快乐抓人」的用法分开。

normal.en: The ending -ive means tending to, so addictive is the quality of tending to create addicts.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ive 意为「有…倾向」，所以 addictive 就是「倾向于制造成瘾者」的性质。

normal.en: The word began with drugs and later spread to games, shows and apps.
normal.cn: 这个词从药物开始，后来扩展到游戏、节目和应用。

normal.en: Addicted describes the person; addictive describes the thing.
normal.cn: addicted 描述人，addictive 描述物。

normal.en: A substance is addictive because stopping it produces real withdrawal.
normal.cn: 一种物质之所以 addictive，是因为停用它会产生真实的戒断反应。

normal.en: A game can be addictive without any chemical at all, because the pull is psychological.
normal.cn: 游戏完全不含化学成分也能让人上瘾，因为那股拉力是心理上的。

abstract.en: A finger tapping the same button without a decision.
abstract.cn: 手指没有经过决定就点了同一个按钮。

abstract.en: One more episode at the edge of midnight.
abstract.cn: 午夜边缘的「再看一集」。

abstract.en: A craving that arrives before the thought of it.
abstract.cn: 渴望先到，念头后到。

examples.en: The game is addictive but harmless.
examples.cn: 这款游戏让人上瘾，但并无害处。

examples.en: Doctors warn that these pills can be addictive.
examples.cn: 医生警告说这些药片可能让人成瘾。

examples.en: Addictive habits are easier to start than to break.
examples.cn: 让人上瘾的习惯，开始容易，戒掉很难。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱得克缇芙」——爱得太深，身体被它克住，怎么也停不下来

root: 由 addict 加形容词词尾 -ive 构成；addict 出自拉丁语 addicere「判归、交付」的过去分词 addictus。十九世纪医学开始用这个词族描述制造依赖的药物，现代又扩展到游戏、节目等一切让人停不下来的东西。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses: one about chemical or behavioural dependence, one about a pleasure that will not release its hold.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项：一个指生理或行为上的依赖，一个指让人无法松手的娱乐吸引力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger already pressing the same button again.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指已经又一次按下同一个按钮。

branches.en: THE DRUG: the substance creates a growing need.
branches.cn: 药物线：物质制造出越来越大的需求。

branches.en: THE DOSE: more is required for the same effect.
branches.cn: 剂量线：要达到同样的效果，需要更多。

branches.en: THE GAME: pleasure alone can hold attention.
branches.cn: 游戏线：单靠乐趣就能抓住注意力。

branches.en: THE SHOW: one episode leads straight into the next.
branches.cn: 剧集线：一集结束，直接接上下一集。

branches.en: THE PULL: in both cases stopping feels like a loss.
branches.cn: 拉力线：在两种情况下，停下来都像是一种损失。

intro.en: A Latin participle meaning handed over took the English ending -ive, which turns a base into a quality that acts on someone.
intro.cn: 一个意为「被交付」的拉丁分词接上英语词尾 -ive，把词基变成一种作用在人身上的性质。

latinIntro.en: The Latin parts belong to the addict family; -ive and the other endings are English additions.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁部件属于 addict 这一族；-ive 等词尾是英语后加的。

items.example: It points the assigning towards the person.
items.exampleCN: 它把「判归」指向那个人。

items.example: It supplies the declaring element of addicere.
items.exampleCN: 它提供 addicere 中「宣布」的成分。

items.example: It is the stem behind the whole English family.
items.exampleCN: 它是整个英语词族背后的词干。

items.example: It turns the act of addicting into the quality addictive.
items.exampleCN: 它把「使人成瘾」这个动作变成性质 addictive。

items.example: It produces addicted.
items.exampleCN: 它产出 addicted。

items.example: It produces addiction.
items.exampleCN: 它产出 addiction。

items.example: It is the base to which -ive is attached.
items.exampleCN: 它是接上 -ive 的词基。

items.example: It makes the adverb addictively.
items.exampleCN: 它构成副词 addictively。

derivatives.zh: 由 addictive 加 -ly 构成，义为「让人上瘾地」
由 addictive 加 -ness 构成，义为「成瘾性」

definition_en: the act of adding something; a person or thing added; the arithmetic operation of combining numbers into a sum
core_image: 账本末尾落下一行新的数字，前面的总数随之改变
scene: 账本上原本只有三笔支出，月底又添了一笔，她把新的这一行写在最下面。The ledger already held three expenses, and at month's end she made one more addition at the bottom of the page.
sceneCN: 这里 addition 指账本上新添的那一笔（第 2 个义项：添加物）；句意为月底账本上又多了一笔支出。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 addere 缩成的动词，义为「添加；相加」
由 addition 加 -al 构成，义为「额外的」
由 additional 加 -ly 构成，义为「此外」
由 add 加 -itive 构成，义为「添加剂」

senses.title: The act of adding
senses.definition: the act of putting something new in with what is already there
senses.definitionCN: 把新东西放进已有东西里的那个动作
senses.example: The addition of a small window changed the whole room.
senses.exampleCN: 添了一扇小窗，整个房间都变了。
senses.why: The noun names the act itself, before anyone asks what was added.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指的是动作本身，还没追问加进去的是什么。

senses.title: The thing added
senses.definition: a person or thing that is added to a group, place or collection
senses.definitionCN: 被加进某个群体、场所或收藏里的人或物
senses.example: Their youngest daughter was a late addition to the family.
senses.exampleCN: 他们最小的女儿是家里后来添的成员。
senses.why: English often moves a noun from the act to the item the act produces.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把一个名词从动作转指动作产生的那件东西。

senses.title: Arithmetic
senses.definition: the operation of combining two or more numbers into a sum
senses.definitionCN: 把两个或更多数字合并成一个和的运算
senses.example: Children learn addition before multiplication.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们先学加法，再学乘法。
senses.why: Arithmetic gives the everyday gesture a fixed name and a written symbol.
senses.whyCN: 算术给这个日常动作一个固定的名称和一个书写符号。

intro.en: addition is the Latin noun of the verb addere, and it reached English through French with the ending that still marks an action.
intro.cn: addition 是动词 addere 的拉丁名词形式，经法语进入英语，词尾至今仍标记「动作」。

items.en: Addere meant to give to or put to, from ad- and dare.
items.cn: addere 意为「给到、放到」，由 ad- 与 dare 构成。

items.en: Additio named the act of adding and the thing that resulted.
items.cn: additio 既指添加这个动作，也指添加的结果。

items.en: French carried the learned noun forward as addicion.
items.cn: 法语把这个学术名词以 addicion 的形式传下去。

items.en: English adopted it with the sense of joining one thing to another.
items.cn: 英语借入后，指把一样东西接到另一样上。

items.en: The schoolroom sense of adding numbers settled in beside the older senses.
items.cn: 课堂里「数字相加」的义项在旧义项旁安定下来。

note.en: The look-alike group is the same Latin family; the near-meaning group is other nouns of joining or enlarging.
note.cn: 形近组是同一个拉丁家族；近义组是其他表示「接上、扩大」的名词。

entries.definition: Extra, added beyond what was expected.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「额外的、附加的」。

entries.definition: A substance added for a particular purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「添加剂」。

entries.definition: To put something with something else.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「添加；相加」，是这一族的词基。

entries.definition: Something added to improve or complete a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「补充物」，强调补足。

entries.definition: The act of putting something inside something else.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「插入」，强调放进内部。

entries.definition: A rise in amount, number or size.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「增长」，强调数量变大。

normalIntro.en: The hooks follow one noun through three uses: the act, the item, and the schoolroom operation.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子跟着同一个名词走过三种用法：动作、物件和课堂运算。

normal.en: addition is the noun of addere, so it names the act behind the verb add.
normal.cn: addition 是 addere 的名词，所以它命名的是动词 add 背后的动作。

normal.en: The ending -ition marks an action or its result, which is why the word can mean both the adding and the thing added.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ition 标记动作或结果，所以这个词既能指「加」也能指「加进去的东西」。

normal.en: In addition is a fixed phrase meaning besides, and in addition to means as well as.
normal.cn: in addition 是固定短语，意为「此外」；in addition to 意为「除…之外还」。

normal.en: A new addition to a family is a person, not a number.
normal.cn: 「a new addition to a family」指的是一个人，不是数字。

normal.en: Addition and subtraction are taught together because they undo each other.
normal.cn: 加法和减法一起教，因为它们互相抵消。

abstract.en: A new line at the bottom of a page, changing the total.
abstract.cn: 页面底部多出一行，总数随之改变。

abstract.en: A chair pulled up to a table that was already full.
abstract.cn: 一把椅子被拉到已经坐满的桌边。

abstract.en: Two columns meeting in a single figure.
abstract.cn: 两列数字汇成一个数。

examples.en: In addition, the store stays open late on Fridays.
examples.cn: 此外，这家店周五营业到很晚。

examples.en: The new wing is a welcome addition to the library.
examples.cn: 新配楼是图书馆一个受欢迎的新增部分。

examples.en: Addition is the first operation children master.
examples.cn: 加法是孩子们最早掌握的运算。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额迪申」——额头上多添一道，就是又加了一样东西

root: 源自拉丁语 addere「给到、加到」的名词形式 additio，经古法语进入英语；词尾 -ition 表示动作或结果，因此这个词同时指「添加的动作」「添加之物」与「加法运算」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: the act, the thing added, and the schoolroom operation.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：添加的动作、被添加的东西、课堂里的加法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one new figure at the foot of a ledger, and the total moves.
core.cn: 核心意象：账本末尾多出一个数字，总数随之移动。

branches.en: THE ACT: the hand places something new in the pile.
branches.cn: 动作线：手把新东西放进那一堆。

branches.en: THE ITEM: what was placed now belongs to the whole.
branches.cn: 物件线：被放进去的东西现在属于整体。

branches.en: THE NEWCOMER: a person can be a late addition to a group.
branches.cn: 新成员线：一个人也可以是团体后来添的成员。

branches.en: THE OPERATION: arithmetic fixes the gesture as a rule.
branches.cn: 运算线：算术把这个动作固定成一条规则。

branches.en: THE TOTAL: joining always leaves the whole larger than before.
branches.cn: 总数线：每一次接合都让整体比原先更大。

items.example: It is the verb behind addition.
items.exampleCN: 它是 addition 背后的动词。

items.example: It is the direct Latin source of addition.
items.exampleCN: 它是 addition 的直接拉丁来源。

items.example: It marks the noun of an action.
items.exampleCN: 它标记一个动作的名词形式。

items.exampleCN: 它构成 additionally。

senses.title: Extra in amount
senses.definition: extra, added on top of an amount that already exists
senses.definitionCN: 在已有数量之上再加的
senses.example: The airline charges an additional fee for extra bags.
senses.exampleCN: 航空公司对超重行李收取额外费用。
senses.why: It measures quantity: what was already enough is now increased.
senses.whyCN: 它衡量的是数量：本来已经够的部分，现在又加了一层。

senses.title: Further support
senses.definition: further, supplied to complete or support what has already been given
senses.definitionCN: 为补全或支持已经给出的内容而另外提供的
senses.example: Additional information is available on the website.
senses.exampleCN: 网站上还有补充信息。
senses.why: The same word moves from quantity to support, where the addition completes rather than merely enlarges.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词从数量转到支撑，这时添加是为了补全，而不只是把量做大。

intro.en: additional is addition plus the adjective ending -al, so it literally means belonging to an adding.
intro.cn: additional 是 addition 加上形容词词尾 -al，字面意思就是「属于添加这件事的」。

items.en: Addere meant to give to, built from ad- and dare.
items.cn: addere 意为「给到」，由 ad- 与 dare 构成。

items.en: Additio named the act of adding and the thing added.
items.cn: additio 指添加的动作，也指添加之物。

items.en: English formed the noun addition and used it for both the act and the result.
items.cn: 英语造出名词 addition，兼指动作与结果。

items.en: The ending -al turned the noun into an adjective meaning relating to.
items.cn: 词尾 -al 把名词变成形容词，意为「与…有关」。

items.en: The adjective settled into two uses, extra quantity and further support.
items.cn: 这个形容词稳定在两个用法上：额外的量，以及进一步的补充。

note.en: The look-alike group is the same Latin family; the near-meaning group is other adjectives of something added.
note.cn: 形近组是同一个拉丁家族；近义组是其他表示「额外添加」的形容词。

entries.definition: The act of adding, or the thing added.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「添加；添加物；加法」。

entries.definition: A substance added for a purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「添加剂」。

entries.definition: To put something with something else.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「添加；相加」。

entries.definition: More than is usual or expected.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「额外的」，最口语化。

entries.definition: Provided to complete or add to something.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「补充的」，强调补足。

entries.definition: Additional, beyond what has already been done.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「进一步的」，强调接着往下。

normalIntro.en: The hooks treat the word as addition wearing an adjective coat.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把这个词看作穿上形容词外衣的 addition。

normal.en: addition plus -al gives additional, so the noun simply becomes a describing word.
normal.cn: addition 加 -al 就是 additional，名词就这样变成了描述词。

normal.en: The core meaning stays the same: something is put with what is already there.
normal.cn: 核心意思没变：有东西被放到已有的东西旁边。

normal.en: Additional fee, additional staff and additional time all point at quantity.
normal.cn: additional fee、additional staff 和 additional time 都指向数量。

normal.en: Additional information is different: it completes a picture rather than enlarging it.
normal.cn: additional information 不一样：它是补全一幅图，而不是把图放大。

normal.en: -ly turns it into additionally, a common way to begin a second point.
normal.cn: 加 -ly 变成 additionally，常用来引出第二点。

abstract.en: A small box set on top of a full crate.
abstract.cn: 一只小盒子被放到装满的箱子上。

abstract.en: One more page slipped into an already stapled report.
abstract.cn: 一页纸被塞进已经装订好的报告。

abstract.en: A second key added to a ring that already jingles.
abstract.cn: 一把新钥匙加到已经叮当作响的钥匙圈上。

examples.en: An additional charge applies to oversized bags.
examples.cn: 超大行李要另收一笔费用。

examples.en: We need additional time to finish the survey.
examples.cn: 我们需要额外的时间完成这项调查。

examples.en: Additional copies are kept in the office.
examples.cn: 办公室还留了额外的副本。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额迪申诺」——额头上再添一道，就是额外多出来的

root: 由 addition 加形容词词尾 -al 构成；addition 出自拉丁语 additio，源自 addere「给到、加到」。因此这个词的字面意思是「属于添加的」，先指数量上的额外，再指信息或支持上的补充。

sensesIntro.en: Two uses: extra quantity, and further material that completes what exists.
sensesIntro.cn: 两种用法：数量上的额外，以及补全现有内容的补充材料。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small box placed on a crate that was already full.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只小盒子被放到本来已经装满的箱子上。

branches.en: THE FEE: a charge is added after the first price.
branches.cn: 费用线：第一笔价钱之后又加了一笔。

branches.en: THE HANDS: extra staff arrive when the first team is short.
branches.cn: 人手线：第一队不够时，额外的人到了。

branches.en: THE NOTE: further information completes the first account.
branches.cn: 说明线：进一步的信息补全了最初的叙述。

branches.en: THE APPENDIX: material is added at the end for support.
branches.cn: 附录线：材料被加在末尾以供支撑。

branches.en: THE WHOLE: the base plus the addition now meets the need.
branches.cn: 整体线：底子加上新增部分，如今满足了需要。

intro.en: The Latin noun additio took the English ending -al, and the result describes anything that belongs to adding.
intro.cn: 拉丁名词 additio 接上英语词尾 -al，结果就是描述「属于添加」的任何东西。

latinIntro.en: ad-, dare and additio are the attested Latin layers; -al and -ly are English.
latinIntro.cn: ad-、dare 与 additio 是有文献可证的拉丁层；-al 与 -ly 是英语层。

items.example: It points the giving towards what is there.
items.exampleCN: 它把「给」指向已经存在的对象。

items.example: It supplies the giving half of addere.
items.exampleCN: 它提供 addere 中「给」的那一半。

items.example: It is the noun behind addition and additional.
items.exampleCN: 它是 addition 与 additional 背后的名词。

items.example: It forms addition from the Latin stem.
items.exampleCN: 它用拉丁词干构成 addition。

items.example: It turns addition into additional.
items.exampleCN: 它把 addition 变成 additional。

items.example: It is the short verb of the family.
items.exampleCN: 它是这一族里短的动词。

items.example: It forms additionally.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 additionally。

items.example: It marks additions in the plural.
items.exampleCN: 它标记 additions 的复数。

derivatives.zh: 由 additional 加 -ly 构成，义为「此外」
同族名词，义为「添加；加法」
同族动词，义为「添加；相加」

definition_zh: 地址；演讲；处理、应对；对…讲话
definition_en: the details of where someone lives or a place is; a formal speech; to deal with a problem; to speak directly to someone
core_image: 信封上一行小字，把人指向一扇具体的门
scene: 信封上的字迹被雨打湿了，邮递员停下来辨认那行地址。Rain had blurred the writing on the envelope, and the postman stopped to make out the address.
sceneCN: 这里 address 指信封上写的住址（第 1 个义项：地址）；句意为雨水模糊了字迹，邮递员停下来辨认地址。

derivatives.zh: 由 address 加 -ee 构成，义为「收件人」
由 address 加 -able 构成，义为「可处理的」
由 address 加 -ing 构成，义为「称呼；处理」

senses.title: Where someone can be reached
senses.definition: the details of a place where someone lives or can be reached
senses.definitionCN: 某人居住或可被联系到的地点的具体信息
senses.example: Write your address clearly on the form.
senses.exampleCN: 在表格上把地址写清楚。
senses.why: The word points at a place by naming the details that locate it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词通过写出定位所需的细节来指向一个地点。

senses.title: A formal speech
senses.definition: a formal speech given to an audience
senses.definitionCN: 面向听众的正式讲话
senses.example: The president gave a short address to the nation.
senses.exampleCN: 总统向全国发表了一次简短演讲。
senses.why: The noun moved from directing words at a place to directing them at people.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词从「把话指向一个地点」转向「把话指向一群人」。

senses.title: To deal with a problem
senses.definition: to deal with a problem, issue or need
senses.definitionCN: 处理某个问题、议题或需求
senses.example: The council must address the housing shortage.
senses.exampleCN: 市议会必须处理住房短缺问题。
senses.why: Here the verb means to turn towards a problem and act on it.
senses.whyCN: 这里的动词意为转向一个问题，并对它采取行动。

senses.title: To speak to someone
senses.definition: to speak directly to a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 直接对某人或某群体说话
senses.example: She addressed the crowd from the steps.
senses.exampleCN: 她站在台阶上对人群讲话。
senses.why: This is the oldest image made literal: words are aimed at someone.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的意象被字面化：话语被对准某个人。

intro.en: address came through French from a Latin verb of straightening and directing, which is why it can mean both a place and the act of aiming words.
intro.cn: address 经法语来自一个表示「弄直、指引」的拉丁动词，所以它既能指一个地点，也能指把话对准某人的动作。

items.en: The prefix meant to or towards, aiming an action at something.
items.cn: 这个前缀意为「向、朝」，把动作对准某物。

items.en: Directus meant straight or direct, from the verb for guiding.
items.cn: directus 意为「直的、直接的」，出自表示引导的动词。

items.en: Adresser meant to direct, to set right, and to equip.
items.cn: adresser 意为指引、扶正，也有装备的意思。

items.en: English used it for setting something straight and for aiming words at a person.
items.cn: 中世纪英语用它表示把东西弄正，也表示把话对准某人。

items.en: The postal sense settled in, and the public speech sense grew beside it.
items.cn: 邮政地址的义项稳定下来，公开演讲的义项在旁边成长。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the address stem; the near-meaning group covers speech and handling.
note.cn: 形近组共享 address 这个词干；近义组覆盖「讲话」与「处理」两条线。

entries.definition: The person to whom a letter is sent.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「收件人」。

entries.definition: Able to be dealt with or reached.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可处理的、可寻址的」。

entries.definition: To correct or make up for something wrong.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「纠正、补偿」，拼写相近但前缀不同。

entries.definition: A talk given to an audience.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「演讲」，是最通用的说法。

entries.definition: A formal talk given to teach or inform.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「讲座」，偏教学。

entries.definition: To make a determined effort to deal with a problem.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「应对、处理」，强调动手解决。

normalIntro.en: The hooks run the word from a written line on an envelope to a voice aimed at a crowd.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子让这个词从信封上的一行字，走到对准人群的声音。

normal.en: The Latin base means straight or direct, so address is about aiming something at a target.
normal.cn: 拉丁词基意为「直的、直接的」，所以 address 是把某物对准一个目标。

normal.en: A postal address aims a letter at one door among many.
normal.cn: 邮政地址把一封信对准许多扇门中的一扇。

normal.en: A speech address aims words at a crowd in the same way.
normal.cn: 演讲同样是把话语对准一群人。

normal.en: To address a problem is to turn towards it instead of avoiding it.
normal.cn: address a problem 就是转向它，而不是回避它。

normal.en: The spelling has a double d and a double s, which many learners drop.
normal.cn: 这个词有两个 d 和两个 s，学习者常漏写。

abstract.en: A line of ink leading a stranger to one door.
abstract.cn: 一行墨迹把一个陌生人引到一扇门前。

abstract.en: A voice turning towards a crowd instead of away.
abstract.cn: 一个声音转向人群，而不是转开。

abstract.en: A problem finally looked at directly.
abstract.cn: 一个问题终于被正面看上一眼。

examples.en: Please send the letter to my new address.
examples.cn: 请把信寄到我的新地址。

examples.en: The mayor addressed the crowd at noon.
examples.cn: 市长在中午对人群讲了话。

examples.en: The report addresses the causes of the shortage.
examples.cn: 这份报告处理了短缺的成因。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额追斯」——额头上追着一条路线，一路找到那个地址

root: 经古法语 adresser 来自拉丁语 ad-「向」与 directus「直的、直接的」；本义是把东西弄正、把话对准某人，后来分化出「地址」「演讲」「处理问题」「对人讲话」等义项。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: a locating line, a formal speech, handling a problem, and speaking to people.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：定位的一行字、正式演讲、处理问题、对人讲话。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of ink on an envelope pointing to one particular door.
core.cn: 核心意象：信封上一行墨迹，指向某一扇具体的门。

branches.en: THE DOOR: the written details locate one home.
branches.cn: 门牌线：写下的细节定位到一个家。

branches.en: THE PODIUM: the speech aims words at many people at once.
branches.cn: 讲台线：演讲把话一次对准许多人。

branches.en: THE DESK: the verb turns towards a problem and works on it.
branches.cn: 案头线：动词转向问题，并对它下功夫。

branches.en: THE VOICE: the oldest sense is simply speaking to someone.
branches.cn: 声音线：最古老的义项就是直接对某人说话。

branches.en: THE TARGET: in every case something is aimed at a chosen point.
branches.cn: 目标线：无论哪种用法，都有东西被对准一个选定的点。

intro.en: A Latin prefix of direction and a Latin adjective meaning straight combine, through French, into a word about aiming at a target.
intro.cn: 一个表示方向的拉丁前缀与一个意为「直」的拉丁形容词，经法语合成一个关于「对准目标」的词。

latinIntro.en: ad- and directus are attested Latin elements; adresser is the Old French link, and the endings are English.
latinIntro.cn: ad- 与 directus 是有文献可证的拉丁成分；adresser 是古法语的中间环节，词尾属于英语。

items.example: It aims the action at a target.
items.exampleCN: 它把动作对准一个目标。

items.example: It supplies the straight-line image behind address.
items.exampleCN: 它提供 address 背后那条直线的意象。

items.example: It is the French form English borrowed.
items.exampleCN: 它是英语借用的法语形式。

items.example: It forms addressee, the person written to.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 addressee，即被写寄的人。

items.example: It forms addressable.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 addressable。

items.example: It marks addresses.
items.exampleCN: 它标记 addresses。

items.example: It produces addressed.
items.exampleCN: 它产出 addressed。

items.example: It produces addressing.
items.exampleCN: 它产出 addressing。

derivatives.zh: 由 address 加 -ee 构成，义为「收件人」
由 address 加 -able 构成，义为「可处理的」
由 address 加 -ing 构成，义为「称呼；处理」

definition_en: enough for a particular purpose; acceptable but not particularly good
core_image: 一只刚好盛满的水杯，离杯口只差一点
scene: 水只够每人一小杯，虽然不宽裕，但解渴是够了。There was only one small cup for each person, not generous, but adequate to quench the thirst.
sceneCN: 这里 adequate 指刚好够用（第 1 个义项：足够的）；句意为水虽不宽裕，但足以解渴。

derivatives.zh: 由 adequate 加 -ly 构成，义为「充分地」
由 adequate 加 -acy 构成，义为「足够、适当」
由 in- 加 adequate 构成，义为「不足的」
由 in- 加 adequacy 构成，义为「不足、欠缺」

senses.title: Enough for the purpose
senses.definition: enough in quantity or quality for the purpose at hand
senses.definitionCN: 在数量或质量上足以应付当前目的
senses.example: The shelter provides adequate food and water.
senses.exampleCN: 收容所提供足够的食物和水。
senses.why: It answers a practical question: is there enough to do the job?
senses.whyCN: 它回答的是一个实际问题：这些东西够不够完成这件事？

senses.title: Merely acceptable
senses.definition: acceptable but not particularly good
senses.definitionCN: 可以接受，但并不特别好
senses.example: The room was clean but only adequate.
senses.exampleCN: 房间干净，但也只是勉强过得去。
senses.why: The same word can lower its aim: enough to pass, not enough to praise.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也能把目标调低：够格通过，但不足以让人称赞。

intro.en: adequate comes from a Latin verb meaning to make equal, so its oldest idea is a balance between what is needed and what is there.
intro.cn: adequate 出自一个意为「使相等」的拉丁动词，它最古老的想法就是「所需」与「所有」之间的平衡。

items.en: Aequus meant level or equal, the root of many words about fairness.
items.cn: aequus 意为「平的、相等的」，是许多表示公平的词根。

items.en: Adaequare meant to make equal to something, to level it with it.
items.cn: adaequare 意为使与某物相等，把它拉到同一水平。

items.en: The participle meant made equal, and so sufficient to match a demand.
items.cn: 分词意为「被弄成相等的」，因而足以匹配一项需求。

items.en: English adopted it for things that equal what is required.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语借入，指与所需相当的事物。

items.en: A weaker sense grew: acceptable, though nothing more.
items.cn: 一个更弱的义项长出来：可以接受，但仅此而已。

note.en: The look-alike group is the same family with its negative; the near-meaning group is other words for enough.
note.cn: 形近组是同一家族及其否定形式；近义组是其他表示「足够」的词。

entries.definition: The quality of being enough.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「足够、适当」。

entries.definition: Not enough for the purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不足的」，是这个词的否定形式。

entries.definition: In a way that is enough.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「充分地」。

entries.definition: Enough, often in a formal or official context.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「充足的」，较正式。

entries.definition: Good enough to be allowed or agreed to.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可接受的」，偏主观评价。

entries.definition: Just good enough, though not excellent.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「还过得去的」，语气最弱。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the Latin picture of leveling: what you have is brought level with what you need.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子保留拉丁语「找平」的画面：你有的被拉到与你所需齐平。

normal.en: The root aequus means equal, so adequate is about a balance between need and supply.
normal.cn: 词根 aequus 意为「相等」，所以 adequate 讲的是需求与供给之间的平衡。

normal.en: Adequate is not a compliment; it says the job can be done, not that it was done well.
normal.cn: adequate 不是夸奖；它说事情能办成，而不是办得漂亮。

normal.en: The negative inadequate is far more common in complaints than adequate is in praise.
normal.cn: 否定形式 inadequate 在抱怨里出现得远比 adequate 在赞美里多。

normal.en: Adequately means to a degree that is enough, no more.
normal.cn: adequately 意为达到够用的程度，仅此而已。

normal.en: Think of a cup filled exactly to the line, not a cup running over.
normal.cn: 想一只刚好倒到刻度线的杯子，而不是溢出来的杯子。

abstract.en: A cup filled to the mark and then stopped.
abstract.cn: 杯子倒到刻度就停手。

abstract.en: A bridge that holds the weight it was built for.
abstract.cn: 一座刚好承得住设计重量的桥。

abstract.en: A meal that ends hunger without being remembered.
abstract.cn: 一顿能止饿、却不会被记住的饭。

examples.en: The lighting in the room is adequate for reading.
examples.cn: 房间里的光线看书够用。

examples.en: They had adequate warning before the storm.
examples.cn: 风暴来临前，他们得到了足够的预警。

examples.en: The result was adequate, though not brilliant.
examples.cn: 结果还算过得去，虽然并不出色。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德夸特」——阿德夸口说这点东西刚好够用

root: 源自拉丁语 adaequare「使相等」，由 ad-「向」与 aequus「平的、相等的」构成；分词 adaequatus 指「被弄成与需求相等」，十七世纪进入英语，先指「足以匹配所需」，后衍生出「尚可、勉强过得去」的弱化义。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses: genuinely enough, and merely acceptable.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项：真正足够，以及仅仅可以接受。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cup filled exactly to the line and then left alone.
core.cn: 核心意象：杯子刚好倒到刻度线，然后就停手。

branches.en: THE NEED: a purpose sets the amount required.
branches.cn: 需求线：一个目的定出了所需的量。

branches.en: THE BALANCE: supply is brought level with that demand.
branches.cn: 平衡线：供给被拉到与那项需求齐平。

branches.en: THE SHRUG: the same word can mean merely passable.
branches.cn: 耸肩线：同一个词也能表示「勉强过得去」。

branches.en: THE UNPRAISED: nothing is wrong, and nothing is memorable.
branches.cn: 无赞线：没有出错，也没有任何值得记住的地方。

branches.en: THE LINE: both uses ask whether the level has been reached.
branches.cn: 刻度线：两种用法都在问，那条线到底有没有达到。

intro.en: A Latin prefix of direction and a Latin adjective meaning equal produced a verb of leveling, and English took its participle as an adjective.
intro.cn: 一个表示方向的拉丁前缀与一个意为「相等」的拉丁形容词造出一个「找平」的动词，英语取其分词作形容词。

latinIntro.en: aequus, adaequare and adaequatus are attested; -ate and the English endings were added later.
latinIntro.cn: aequus、adaequare 与 adaequatus 都有文献可证；-ate 与英语词尾是后来加的。

items.example: It directs the leveling towards a standard.
items.exampleCN: 它把「找平」这个动作指向一个标准。

items.example: It supplies the balance at the heart of adequate.
items.exampleCN: 它提供 adequate 核心处的平衡意象。

items.example: It is the verb behind the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个形容词背后的动词。

items.example: It is the form English took as an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它是英语拿来当形容词用的形式。

items.example: It gives the word its adjective shape.
items.exampleCN: 它给这个词形容词的外形。

items.example: It forms adequately.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 adequately。

items.example: It forms adequacy.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 adequacy。

items.example: It forms inadequate.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 inadequate。

由 adequate 加 -acy 构成，义为「足够、适当」
