definition_en: to stick firmly to a surface; to follow a rule or belief closely
core_image: 一片叶子紧紧贴在被雨水打湿的玻璃上
scene: 雨后的玻璃上，一片叶子怎么也甩不掉，牢牢粘在表面。After the rain, a leaf would not shake off the window; it adhered to the wet glass.
sceneCN: 这里 adhere 指物体粘在表面上（第 1 个义项：粘附）；句意为雨后叶子牢牢粘在湿玻璃上。

derivatives.zh: 由 adhere 加 -sion 构成，义为「粘附、附着力」
由 adhere 加 -ive 构成，义为「粘合剂」
由 adhere 加 -ence 构成，义为「遵守、坚持」
由 adhere 加 -ent 构成，义为「拥护者」

senses.title: To stick to a surface
senses.definition: to stick firmly to a surface or to another substance
senses.definitionCN: 牢牢粘在某个表面或另一种物质上
senses.example: The tape will adhere to almost any clean surface.
senses.exampleCN: 这种胶带几乎能粘在任何干净的表面。
senses.why: This is the physical root: two things are held together along their boundary.
senses.whyCN: 这是物理上的本义：两样东西沿着接触的边界被固定在一起。

senses.title: To follow a rule
senses.definition: to follow a rule, agreement or belief closely
senses.definitionCN: 紧密遵循某条规则、协议或信念
senses.example: All members must adhere to the code of conduct.
senses.exampleCN: 所有成员都必须遵守行为准则。
senses.why: The metaphor treats a rule as a surface the person chooses to stay attached to.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把规则当成一个表面，人选择一直贴在上面。

intro.en: adhere is Latin adhaerere, to stick to, and the rule sense is the same physical image applied to conduct.
intro.cn: adhere 是拉丁语 adhaerere「粘到」，规则义项只是把同一个物理画面用到行为上。

items.en: Haerere meant to stick, to cling, or to remain fixed.
items.cn: haerere 意为粘住、附着、固定不动。

items.en: The prefix ad- added direction: to stick to something.
items.cn: 前缀 ad- 加上方向：粘到某物上。

items.en: The noun adhaesio named the state of being stuck together.
items.cn: 名词 adhaesio 指被粘在一起的状态。

items.en: English borrowed adhere for physical sticking and for holding to an opinion.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语借入 adhere，既指物理粘附，也指坚持某种看法。

items.en: The rule and agreement sense became the most common in official writing.
items.cn: 规则与协议的义项在正式文本里变得最常见。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the sticking root; the near-meaning group splits into physical and moral sticking.
note.cn: 形近组共享「粘住」这个词根；近义组分成物理粘附与道义坚持两条线。

entries.definition: The state or force of being stuck to something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「粘附、附着力」。

entries.definition: A substance that holds things together.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「粘合剂」，也可作形容词。

entries.definition: The act of following a rule closely.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「遵守、坚持」。

entries.definition: To become fixed to a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「粘住」，最日常的说法。

entries.definition: To hold on tightly to something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「紧抓、附着」，强调不肯松开。

entries.definition: To act in accordance with a rule or request.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「遵从」，只用于规则与要求。

normalIntro.en: The hooks begin with a leaf on wet glass and end with a member obeying a code.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从湿玻璃上的叶子开始，到一名成员遵守准则结束。

normal.en: The Latin verb haerere means to stick, and ad- means to, so adhere is to stick to.
normal.cn: 拉丁动词 haerere 意为「粘」，ad- 意为「向」，所以 adhere 就是「粘到」。

normal.en: The physical sense is first: a label, a leaf, a patch on a surface.
normal.cn: 物理义项在先：标签、叶子、贴在表面上的补丁。

normal.en: The moral sense reuses the same picture: a person stays attached to a rule.
normal.cn: 道义义项复用同一幅画：一个人一直贴在一条规则上。

normal.en: Adherence is the noun for following rules, and adhesion is the noun for sticking.
normal.cn: adherence 是「遵守规则」的名词，adhesion 是「粘附」的名词。

normal.en: Adhesive tape is named by the same root, which makes the family easy to remember.
normal.cn: adhesive tape 用的也是同一个词根，这一族因此很好记。

abstract.en: A wet leaf refusing to leave the glass.
abstract.cn: 一片湿叶子不肯离开玻璃。

abstract.en: A promise kept even when no one is watching.
abstract.cn: 一个没人监督也守住的承诺。

abstract.en: Two surfaces meeting and not letting go.
abstract.cn: 两个表面贴在一起，不肯松开。

examples.en: The sticker adhered to the glass for years.
examples.cn: 那张贴纸在玻璃上粘了很多年。

examples.en: Members are expected to adhere to the rules.
examples.cn: 成员应当遵守规则。

examples.en: Dust adheres easily to the screen.
examples.cn: 灰尘很容易附着在屏幕上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额嘿尔」——额头上贴住一块东西，怎么也不掉

root: 源自拉丁语 adhaerere「粘到」，由 ad-「向」与 haerere「粘、附着」构成；本义是物体贴附在表面上，十七世纪起引申为坚持某种意见、遵守某条规则或协议。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses: physical sticking, and keeping close to a rule or belief.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项：物理上的粘附，以及紧紧守住规则或信念。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wet leaf holding fast to a window pane.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片湿叶子牢牢贴在窗玻璃上。

branches.en: THE GLASS: the leaf meets the pane and stays.
branches.cn: 玻璃线：叶子碰到玻璃，然后留了下来。

branches.en: THE TAPE: an adhesive holds two surfaces at their edge.
branches.cn: 胶带线：粘合剂把两个表面固定在交界处。

branches.en: THE CODE: a member stays attached to the rules.
branches.cn: 准则线：成员一直贴在规则上。

branches.en: THE BELIEF: a person refuses to let go of a principle.
branches.cn: 信念线：一个人不肯松开一条原则。

branches.en: THE GRIP: in both cases the word means not letting go.
branches.cn: 抓握线：两种情况下，这个词都表示「不松开」。

intro.en: A Latin prefix of direction and a Latin verb of sticking formed adhaerere, and English built a whole family of nouns and adjectives on it.
intro.cn: 一个表示方向的拉丁前缀与一个表示「粘」的拉丁动词构成 adhaerere，英语又在上面造出一整族名词与形容词。

latinIntro.en: haerere, adhaerere and adhaesio are attested; the English endings came later.
latinIntro.cn: haerere、adhaerere 与 adhaesio 都有文献可证；英语词尾是后来加的。

items.exampleCN: 它把「粘」变成「粘到某物上」。

items.example: It is the stuck core of the word.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个词里「粘住」的核心。

items.example: It is the direct source of adhere.
items.exampleCN: 它是 adhere 的直接来源。

items.exampleCN: 它产出 adhered。

definition_en: next to or adjoining something; (of angles) sharing a common side and vertex
core_image: 两栋房子共用一道墙，门牌挨着门牌
scene: 两户人家的院子只隔一道矮篱笆，孩子从一边就能翻到另一边。The two gardens were separated only by a low fence, and the children could climb from one to the other because the yards were adjacent.
sceneCN: 这里 adjacent 指紧挨着的（第 1 个义项：邻近的）；句意为两个院子只隔一道矮篱笆，彼此紧挨。

derivatives.zh: 由 adjacent 加 -cy 构成，义为「邻近、毗连」
由 adjacent 加 -ly 构成，义为「相邻地」

senses.title: Next to something
senses.definition: lying next to or sharing a boundary with something
senses.definitionCN: 紧挨着某物，或与它共享一条边界
senses.example: The hotel is adjacent to the station.
senses.exampleCN: 这家旅馆紧挨着车站。
senses.why: It describes position at a shared edge, not distance in general.
senses.whyCN: 它描述的是共享一条边时的位置关系，而不是笼统的距离。

senses.title: Sharing a side, in geometry
senses.definition: sharing a common side and vertex, as of two angles
senses.definitionCN: 两个角共用一条边和一个顶点
senses.example: The two adjacent angles add up to a right angle.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个邻角加起来是一个直角。
senses.why: Geometry keeps the same edge-sharing idea but moves it into a figure.
senses.whyCN: 几何保留了同一个「共边」的想法，只是把它搬进一个图形里。

intro.en: adjacent comes from a Latin verb meaning to lie beside, so its whole history is about sharing an edge.
intro.cn: adjacent 出自一个意为「躺在旁边」的拉丁动词，它整段历史都围绕「共享一条边」。

items.en: Jacere meant to lie or to be thrown down.
items.cn: jacere 意为躺下，或被投下。

items.en: With ad-, the verb meant to lie beside or near.
items.cn: 加上 ad- 之后，这个动词意为躺在旁边或近处。

items.en: The participle meant lying beside, and English took it as an adjective.
items.cn: 分词意为「躺在旁边的」，英语把它作形容词借走。

items.en: It entered English for places and properties that touch.
items.cn: 十七世纪进入英语，指彼此相接的地点与地产。

items.en: Geometry gave the word a precise sense for angles sharing a side.
items.cn: 几何学给这个词一个精确义项，专指共边的角。

note.en: The look-alike group is the adjoining family; the near-meaning group is other words for next to.
note.cn: 形近组是 adjoin 这一族；近义组是其他表示「在旁边」的词。

entries.definition: The state of being next to something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「邻近、毗连」。

entries.definition: Next to and usually touching.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「毗连的」，强调相接。

entries.definition: To be next to and touch something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「毗连、紧挨」。

entries.definition: Located nearby, especially of places.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「邻近的」，偏地理范围。

entries.definition: Not far away.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「附近的」，不要求相接。

entries.definition: Sharing a border with something.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「接壤的」，多用于国家与地区。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of two plots sharing one line, then extend it to angles.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子保留两块地共享一条线的画面，再把它延伸到角上。

normal.en: The Latin verb jacere means to lie, and ad- means beside, so adjacent is lying beside.
normal.cn: 拉丁动词 jacere 意为「躺」，ad- 意为「在旁边」，所以 adjacent 就是「躺在旁边」。

normal.en: Adjacent is stronger than nearby: the two things must share an edge.
normal.cn: adjacent 比 nearby 更强：两样东西必须共享一条边。

normal.en: Adjacent rooms are not merely close; a wall runs between them.
normal.cn: adjacent rooms 不只是近，中间还有一道共用的墙。

normal.en: In geometry, adjacent angles share a side and a vertex, no wall needed.
normal.cn: 在几何里，邻角共享一条边和一个顶点，不需要墙。

normal.en: The noun adjacency names the relationship, which is useful in graphs and maps.
normal.cn: 名词 adjacency 命名这种关系，在图论和地图里很有用。

abstract.en: Two door plates almost touching on the same wall.
abstract.cn: 同一面墙上两块几乎碰在一起的门牌。

abstract.en: A fence that is the only line between two gardens.
abstract.cn: 一道篱笆，是两个院子之间唯一的线。

abstract.en: Two angles leaning on one shared side.
abstract.cn: 两个角靠在同一条共用的边上。

examples.en: The kitchen is adjacent to the dining room.
examples.cn: 厨房与餐厅相邻。

examples.en: Fire spread quickly to the adjacent buildings.
examples.cn: 火势迅速蔓延到相邻的建筑。

examples.en: Adjacent angles share a common side.
examples.cn: 邻角共享一条公共边。

root: 源自拉丁语 adjacere「躺在旁边」，由 ad-「向、旁」与 jacere「躺」构成；分词 adjacens 被英语借作形容词，先指地点、地产彼此相接，后由几何学赋予「共边共顶点」的精确义项。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses: physical neighbours sharing an edge, and angles sharing a side.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项：共享一条边的实体邻居，以及共享一条边的角。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two gardens divided by one low fence.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个院子被一道矮篱笆分开。

branches.en: THE FENCE: two plots meet along a single line.
branches.cn: 篱笆线：两块地在同一条线上相接。

branches.en: THE WALL: adjacent rooms share masonry, not just distance.
branches.cn: 墙线：相邻的房间共享砖墙，而不只是距离近。

branches.en: THE VERTEX: two angles meet at one point.
branches.cn: 顶点线：两个角在一个点上相接。

branches.en: THE SIDE: the shared line is what makes the angles adjacent.
branches.cn: 边线：正是那条共用的线让两个角成为邻角。

branches.en: THE SHARED LINE: every use depends on one common boundary.
branches.cn: 共线：每一种用法都依赖一条共同的边界。

intro.en: A Latin prefix of proximity and a Latin verb of lying formed adjacere, whose participle English borrowed as an adjective.
intro.cn: 一个表示邻近的拉丁前缀与一个表示「躺」的拉丁动词构成 adjacere，英语借其分词作形容词。

latinIntro.en: jacere, adjacere and adjacens are attested; -cy and -ly are English endings.
latinIntro.cn: jacere、adjacere 与 adjacens 都有文献可证；-cy 与 -ly 是英语词尾。

items.example: It supplies the lying image.

items.exampleCN: 它是 adjacent 背后的动词。

items.example: It forms adjacently.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 adjacently。

definition_en: to be next to and often touching something; to attach something as an addition
core_image: 两块地皮在地图上共用一条细线
scene: 那块空地紧挨着学校操场，只隔着一道铁丝网。The empty lot adjoined the school playground, separated only by a wire fence.
sceneCN: 这里 adjoin 指与…毗连（第 1 个义项：紧挨着）；句意为空地紧挨着学校操场，只隔一道铁丝网。

derivatives.zh: 由 adjoin 加 -ing 构成，义为「毗连的」
同族形容词，义为「邻近的」
同族名词，义为「邻近、毗连」

senses.title: To be next to
senses.definition: to be next to and usually touch something
senses.definitionCN: 紧挨着某物，通常还与之接触
senses.example: Their farm adjoins the river.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的农场紧挨着那条河。
senses.why: The verb is positional: two pieces of land share an edge.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词是位置性的：两块土地共享一条边。

senses.title: To attach as an addition
senses.definition: to attach or add something to another thing
senses.definitionCN: 把某物附加到另一物上
senses.example: A small chapel was adjoined to the old church.
senses.exampleCN: 一座小礼拜堂被附建在旧教堂旁。
senses.why: The older sense is joining, and English kept it for physical attachments.
senses.whyCN: 更早的义项就是「连接」，英语把它保留给实体附着。

intro.en: adjoin came through French from a Latin verb that simply meant to join to, and it still keeps that literal force.
intro.cn: adjoin 经法语来自一个意思就是「连接上去」的拉丁动词，至今仍保留这种字面力量。

items.en: Jungere meant to join or yoke, the source of junction and conjunction.
items.cn: jungere 意为连接、套轭，是 junction 与 conjunction 的来源。

items.en: With ad-, it meant to join one thing to another.
items.cn: 加上 ad- 后，意为把一样东西连接到另一样上。

items.en: French carried the verb forward as ajoindre, to join or to be next to.
items.cn: 法语把它传成 ajoindre，意为连接或紧挨。

items.en: English adopted it for land and buildings that touch.
items.cn: 中世纪英语借入，用于相接的土地与建筑。

items.en: The word stayed formal and mostly appears in descriptions of property.
items.cn: 这个词保持正式，主要出现在对地产的描述里。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the joining root; the near-meaning group is other verbs of touching or bordering.
note.cn: 形近组共享「连接」这个词根；近义组是其他表示接触或接壤的动词。

entries.definition: Next to or sharing a boundary.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「邻近的」。

entries.definition: Touching or next to something.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「毗连的」。

entries.definition: A joining together, or a word that joins clauses.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「连接；连词」，与 adjoin 同根。

entries.definition: To share a border with a place.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「与…接壤」，多用于国家与地区。

entries.definition: To be in physical contact with something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「接触」，强调碰到。

entries.definition: To join two things together.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「连接」，强调建立联系。

normalIntro.en: The hooks reduce the word to its join root, then put it back on a map.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把词还原成「连接」这个词根，再把它放回地图上。

normal.en: Jungere means to join, and ad- means to, so adjoin is to join on.
normal.cn: jungere 意为「连接」，ad- 意为「向」，所以 adjoin 就是「接到上面」。

normal.en: The commonest use is about land: a lot adjoins a playground.
normal.cn: 最常见的用法是关于土地：一块地紧挨着操场。

normal.en: Adjoining rooms share a wall and are often connected by a door.
normal.cn: adjoining rooms 共享一道墙，常有一扇门相通。

normal.en: The verb is formal; in speech people usually say next to.
normal.cn: 这个动词偏正式；口语里人们通常说 next to。

normal.en: It shares the root of junction and conjunction, which all involve joining.
normal.cn: 它与 junction、conjunction 同根，都跟「连接」有关。

abstract.en: Two plots sharing one thin line on a map.
abstract.cn: 地图上两块地共享一条细线。

abstract.en: A chapel built against an older wall.
abstract.cn: 一座贴着旧墙建起的小礼拜堂。

abstract.en: A door that connects two rooms without a corridor.
abstract.cn: 一扇不经走廊、直接连通两个房间的门。

examples.en: The garden adjoins the neighbour's wall.
examples.cn: 花园紧挨着邻居家的墙。

examples.en: Two adjoining rooms were turned into one.
examples.cn: 两个相连的房间被合并成一个。

examples.en: A garage adjoins the house.
examples.cn: 车库与房子相连。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额乔因」——额头挨着乔因，两个人紧靠在一起

root: 经古法语 ajoindre 来自拉丁语 adjungere「连接到」，由 ad-「向」与 jungere「连接」构成；本义是把东西接上去，后来主要用于土地、房屋彼此毗连。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses: land or buildings touching, and an addition attached to something.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项：土地或房屋彼此相接，以及把某物附建到另一物上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two plots of land sharing one thin line on a map.
core.cn: 核心意象：地图上两块土地共享一条细线。

branches.en: THE RIVER: the farm stops where the water begins.
branches.cn: 河线：农场在水开始的地方结束。

branches.en: THE FENCE: the lot and the playground share wire.
branches.cn: 铁丝网线：空地与操场共享同一道铁丝网。

branches.en: THE CHAPEL: an addition is built against an older wall.
branches.cn: 礼拜堂线：一个附加部分贴着旧墙建起。

branches.en: THE GARAGE: a new structure joins the house.
branches.cn: 车库线：一座新建筑接到房子上。

branches.en: THE JOINT: every use turns on one thing meeting another.
branches.cn: 接合线：每一种用法都归结为一样东西与另一样接上。

intro.en: The Latin verb jungere, to join, took the prefix ad- and passed through French into English as adjoin.
intro.cn: 拉丁动词 jungere「连接」加上前缀 ad-，经法语进入英语，成为 adjoin。

latinIntro.en: jungere and adjungere are attested; ajoindre is the French link, and the endings are English.
latinIntro.cn: jungere 与 adjungere 都有文献可证；ajoindre 是法语中间环节，词尾属于英语。

items.example: It directs the joining towards a neighbour.
items.exampleCN: 它把「连接」指向相邻的一方。

items.example: It is the joining root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 它是这一族里「连接」的词根。

items.example: It is the direct Latin source.
items.exampleCN: 它是直接的拉丁来源。

items.example: It forms adjoining.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 adjoining。

items.example: It produces adjoined.
items.exampleCN: 它产出 adjoined。

items.example: It produces adjoins.
items.exampleCN: 它产出 adjoins。

items.example: It is the short English cousin of jungere.
items.exampleCN: 它是 jungere 在英语里的短亲。

items.example: It forms junction and conjunction.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 junction 与 conjunction。

同族形容词，义为「邻近的」
同族名词，义为「邻近、毗连」

definition_en: to change something slightly so that it fits or works better; to get used to new conditions
core_image: 一只旋钮被轻轻转了半圈，画面终于清楚
scene: 投影仪的画面偏了一点，他伸手转动镜头旁的小旋钮，直到字变清晰。The image was slightly off, so he turned the small knob beside the lens until the words came into focus and adjusted the projector.
sceneCN: 这里 adjust 指把设备调到合适状态（第 1 个义项：调整、调节）；句意为画面偏了，他转动旋钮把投影仪调清楚。

derivatives.zh: 由 adjust 加 -ment 构成，义为「调整；适应」
由 adjust 加 -able 构成，义为「可调节的」
由 adjust 加 -ed 构成，义为「调整过的」
由 adjust 加 -er 构成，义为「调节器；理赔员」

senses.title: A small change to fit
senses.definition: to change something slightly so that it fits, works or looks better
senses.definitionCN: 略微改变某物，使它更合适、更有效或更好看
senses.example: She adjusted the mirror before driving off.
senses.exampleCN: 她开车前调了调后视镜。
senses.why: The core action is a small turn or shift, not a complete replacement.
senses.whyCN: 这个核心动作是轻轻转一下、挪一点，而不是整个换掉。

senses.title: To adapt to new conditions
senses.definition: to get used to a new situation or environment
senses.definitionCN: 适应新的情况或环境
senses.example: It took him a month to adjust to the night shift.
senses.exampleCN: 他花了一个月才适应夜班。
senses.why: The same word turns inward: here the person, not the object, is what changes.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词转向内部：这时改变的是人，而不是被调整的东西。

senses.title: To set a device
senses.definition: to set a device or control to a particular position
senses.definitionCN: 把设备或控制器调到某个位置
senses.example: Adjust the thermostat to twenty degrees.
senses.exampleCN: 把恒温器调到二十度。
senses.why: Machines gave the verb a precise, repeatable sense with dials and settings.
senses.whyCN: 机器给了这个动词一个精确、可重复的义项，与旋钮和设置有关。

intro.en: adjust came through French from a Latin idea of bringing things close and setting them in order.
intro.cn: adjust 经法语来自一个拉丁想法：把东西带到近处，并把它们安排整齐。

items.en: Juxta meant near or close beside.
items.cn: juxta 意为靠近、在旁边。

items.en: The compound meant to bring close and to put in proper order.
items.cn: 这个复合词意为带到近处，并摆到正确的位置。

items.en: French used it for arranging and setting things right.
items.cn: 法语用它表示安排、把东西弄妥。

items.en: English took the verb for putting affairs or objects into order.
items.cn: 中世纪英语借入这个动词，指把事务或物件安排妥当。

items.en: Machines and daily adaptation widened the range of things one can adjust.
items.cn: 机器与日常适应扩大了「可以调整」的对象范围。

note.en: The look-alike group is the same noun and adjective family; the near-meaning group is other verbs of small change.
note.cn: 形近组是同一族的名词与形容词；近义组是其他表示「小改动」的动词。

entries.definition: A small change made to improve something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「调整；适应」。

entries.definition: Able to be changed to different positions.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可调节的」。

entries.definition: A person or device that adjusts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「调节器；理赔员」。

entries.definition: To change something, often to improve it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「修改」，改动可以较大。

entries.definition: To change in order to suit new conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「适应、改造」，强调适应环境。

entries.definition: To adjust a device for the best performance.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「调校」，多用于仪器与发动机。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the small turn at the centre, then follow it outward into habits and machines.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把「轻轻一转」放在中心，再把它延伸到习惯与机器。

normal.en: The Latin word juxta means near, so adjust is to bring something to where it belongs.
normal.cn: 拉丁词 juxta 意为「靠近」，所以 adjust 就是把东西带到它该在的位置。

normal.en: Adjust is always a matter of degree: a little turn, a little shift.
normal.cn: adjust 总是程度问题：转一点，挪一点。

normal.en: You adjust a mirror, a seat or a volume, and the change is visible at once.
normal.cn: 你调后视镜、座椅或音量，变化立刻看得见。

normal.en: You also adjust to a night shift, and there the change is inside you.
normal.cn: 你也会 adjust to 夜班，这时改变发生在你内部。

normal.en: The adjective adjustable marks anything with a knob or a setting.
normal.cn: 形容词 adjustable 标记一切带旋钮或带设置的东西。

abstract.en: A knob turning half a circle and the picture clearing.
abstract.cn: 旋钮转半圈，画面就清楚了。

abstract.en: A chair lowered until the desk feels right.
abstract.cn: 椅子调低到桌子高度刚好合适。

abstract.en: A body slowly learning a new sleep schedule.
abstract.cn: 身体慢慢学会新的作息。

examples.en: Adjust the seat before you start the car.
examples.cn: 开车前先调好座位。

examples.en: It took her weeks to adjust to the new city.
examples.cn: 她花了好几周才适应这座新城市。

examples.en: He adjusted the volume when the music grew loud.
examples.cn: 音乐变响时，他把音量调低了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额加斯特」——额头上加一点，刚好调到合适

root: 经古法语 adjuster 来自拉丁语，与 juxta「靠近」同源：本义是把东西带到近处、摆到正确的位置，后来指对物件或设备作小幅改动，也指人适应新的环境。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: a small physical change, an inner adaptation, and the setting of a device.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：小幅的物理改动、内在的适应、对设备的调节。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a knob turned half a circle until the image sharpens.
core.cn: 核心意象：旋钮转了半圈，画面就清晰了。

branches.en: THE MIRROR: one small angle makes the road visible.
branches.cn: 后视镜线：一个小角度让道路可见。

branches.en: THE KNOB: the device is set to a chosen position.
branches.cn: 旋钮线：设备被调到选定的位置。

branches.en: THE NIGHT SHIFT: the body slowly rewrites its clock.
branches.cn: 夜班线：身体慢慢改写自己的时钟。

branches.en: THE NEW CITY: habits are rebuilt around unfamiliar streets.
branches.cn: 新城市线：习惯围绕陌生的街道重建。

branches.en: THE BALANCE: every use aims at a better fit.
branches.cn: 平衡线：每一种用法都指向更合适的匹配。

intro.en: A Latin word for near gave French and English a verb of setting things into their proper place.
intro.cn: 一个意为「靠近」的拉丁词，给法语和英语提供了一个「把东西摆到合适位置」的动词。

latinIntro.en: juxta is the attested Latin element; the verb shape came through French, and the endings are English.
latinIntro.cn: juxta 是有文献可证的拉丁成分；动词外形经法语而来，词尾属于英语。

items.example: It moves the object towards its proper place.
items.exampleCN: 它把对象移向它该在的位置。

items.example: It supplies the idea of bringing close.
items.exampleCN: 它提供「带到近处」这个想法。

items.example: It is the French form English borrowed.
items.exampleCN: 它是英语借用的法语形式。

items.example: It forms adjustment.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 adjustment。

items.example: It forms adjustable.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 adjustable。

items.example: It forms adjuster.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 adjuster。

由 adjust 加 -able 构成，义为「可调节的」

definition_en: a small change made so that something works or fits better; the process of getting used to a new situation; an amount added or subtracted to settle an account
core_image: 钟摆被拨动一格，整座钟重新走准
scene: 搬家后的头几周，他每天都要改一改作息，慢慢才睡得好。In the first weeks after moving, he made small adjustments to his routine every day before he could sleep well.
sceneCN: 这里 adjustment 指对作息做的调整（第 1 个义项：调整）；句意为搬家后他每天微调作息，慢慢才睡得好。

derivatives.zh: 词基动词，义为「调整；适应」
由 adjust 加 -able 构成，义为「可调节的」
由 adjust 加 -er 构成，义为「调节器；理赔员」

senses.title: A small change
senses.definition: a small change made to something so that it works or fits better
senses.definitionCN: 为使某物更好用、更合适而做的小改动
senses.example: A slight adjustment to the lens sharpened the image.
senses.exampleCN: 镜头稍微调了一下，画面就清楚了。
senses.why: The noun names the change itself, and it is usually a matter of a little.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指改动本身，而且通常只是「一点点」的事。

senses.title: The process of adapting
senses.definition: the process of getting used to a new situation
senses.definitionCN: 适应新处境的过程
senses.example: The adjustment to city life took months.
senses.exampleCN: 适应城市生活花了好几个月。
senses.why: The same noun can name a slow inner process rather than a single turn.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词也能指缓慢的内在过程，而不是一次转动。

senses.title: A settling difference
senses.definition: an amount added or subtracted in order to settle an account
senses.definitionCN: 为结清账目而增加或扣除的金额
senses.example: The final bill included an adjustment for the extra night.
senses.exampleCN: 最终账单里包含了多住一晚的差额调整。
senses.why: Accounting uses the word for the correcting figure that makes two totals agree.
senses.whyCN: 会计用这个词指那个让两个总数对上的修正数字。

intro.en: adjustment is the noun of adjust, and the -ment ending turns the act of setting right into a countable thing.
intro.cn: adjustment 是 adjust 的名词形式，词尾 -ment 把「弄妥当」这个动作变成一个可以计数的事物。

items.en: Juxta meant near, the seed of the idea of putting things in place.
items.cn: juxta 意为「靠近」，是「把东西摆到位」这个想法的种子。

items.en: French used the verb for arranging and correcting.
items.cn: 法语用这个动词表示安排与校正。

items.en: English formed the verb and used it for objects and for people.
items.cn: 英语造出动词，既用于物件，也用于人。

items.en: The ending -ment made a noun of the action or its result.
items.cn: 词尾 -ment 把动作或其结果变成名词。

items.en: Business and insurance added the sense of a settling figure.
items.cn: 商业与保险又添上「结算数字」的义项。

note.en: The look-alike group is the adjust family; the near-meaning group is other nouns of change and adaptation.
note.cn: 形近组是 adjust 这一族；近义组是其他表示改变与适应的名词。

entries.definition: To make a small change so something fits better.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「调整；适应」。

entries.definition: Able to be set to different positions.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可调节的」。

entries.definition: A device or person that adjusts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「调节器；理赔员」。

entries.definition: A difference from what was before.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「改变」，最宽泛的说法。

entries.definition: A change made to improve or alter something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「修改」，改动可以较大。

entries.definition: The process of becoming suited to new conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「适应、改编」，强调适应过程。

normalIntro.en: The hooks move from one tweak of a lens to a whole account being settled.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从镜头上的一下微调，走到一整笔账被结清。

normal.en: Adjustment is adjust plus -ment, so it turns the verb into a thing you can count.
normal.cn: adjustment 是 adjust 加 -ment，于是动词变成可以计数的事物。

normal.en: A slight adjustment to a lens, a seat or a plan is still a small change.
normal.cn: 对镜头、座椅或计划作 slight adjustment，仍然是小改动。

normal.en: Adjustment to a new country is slower than adjustment to a new chair.
normal.cn: 适应一个新国家，比调整一把新椅子慢得多。

normal.en: In business, an adjustment is the figure that makes two totals agree.
normal.cn: 在商业里，adjustment 是让两个总数对上的那个数字。

normal.en: The plural adjustments often appears in lists of changes after a review.
normal.cn: 复数 adjustments 常出现在复审后列出的改动清单里。

abstract.en: A pendulum nudged one notch and the clock corrected.
abstract.cn: 钟摆被拨动一格，钟就准了。

abstract.en: A new routine rebuilt one small habit at a time.
abstract.cn: 新作息一次重建一个小习惯。

abstract.en: One correcting line at the bottom of a bill.
abstract.cn: 账单底部一行用来修正的数字。

examples.en: The plan needs a small adjustment.
examples.cn: 这个计划需要一点小调整。

examples.en: Her adjustment to the new school was slow.
examples.cn: 她适应新学校的过程很慢。

examples.en: The bill included an adjustment for the extra night.
examples.cn: 账单里包含了多住一晚的差额调整。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额加斯特门特」——额头上加一点，调成刚刚好

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: a small change, an inner adaptation, and a settling figure in accounts.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：小幅改动、内在适应、账目上的结算差额。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pendulum nudged one notch until the clock runs true.
core.cn: 核心意象：钟摆被拨动一格，钟重新走准。

branches.en: THE LENS: one turn brings the picture into focus.
branches.cn: 镜头线：转一下，画面就对焦了。

branches.en: THE PLAN: one clause is changed after review.
branches.cn: 计划线：复审后改掉一个条款。

branches.en: THE ROUTINE: a newcomer rebuilds a daily rhythm.
branches.cn: 作息线：新来的人重建日常节奏。

branches.en: THE CITY: the body learns unfamiliar streets.
branches.cn: 城市线：身体记住陌生的街道。

branches.en: THE BILL: a correcting figure makes the totals agree.
branches.cn: 账单线：一个修正数字让总数对上。

intro.en: The English suffix -ment turns the verb adjust into the countable result of adjusting.
intro.cn: 英语词尾 -ment 把动词 adjust 变成「调整的结果」这个可数名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin element is juxta, near; the verb came through French, and -ment is English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁成分是意为「靠近」的 juxta；动词经法语而来，-ment 属于英语。

definition_en: to manage the affairs of an organization; to put a law, system or test into effect; to give a drug or treatment
core_image: 一个人站在桌后，把事务一件件分派下去
scene: 项目出了乱子，负责人连夜重新分工，把人和钱都管了起来。When the project fell into disorder, the manager redistributed the work overnight and began to administer the whole operation.
sceneCN: 这里 administer 指管理整个项目（第 1 个义项：管理）；句意为项目混乱后，负责人连夜重新分工并接管管理。

derivatives.zh: 由 administer 加 -ation 构成，义为「管理；行政部门」
由 administrate 加 -ive 构成，义为「行政的」
由 administrate 加 -or 构成，义为「管理者」
同根名词，义为「部长；牧师」

senses.title: To manage affairs
senses.definition: to manage the affairs of an organization or project
senses.definitionCN: 管理一个组织或项目的事务
senses.example: She administers a small charity.
senses.exampleCN: 她管理一家小型慈善机构。
senses.why: The word puts someone behind a desk, directing what others do.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把人放到桌子后面，指挥别人去做事。

senses.title: To put into effect
senses.definition: to put a law, system or test into effect
senses.definitionCN: 使法律、制度或考试付诸实施
senses.example: The court administers justice without delay.
senses.exampleCN: 法院毫不拖延地执行司法。
senses.why: Management becomes action: rules are carried out, not merely discussed.

senses.title: To give a drug

senses.example: The nurse administered the vaccine to each child.
senses.exampleCN: 护士给每个孩子接种了疫苗。
senses.why: Medicine borrowed the word for the controlled giving of a remedy.

intro.en: administer is built on the Latin word for a servant, so managing and giving were originally acts of service.
intro.cn: administer 长在拉丁语「仆人」这个词上，所以「管理」和「给予」最初都是服务性的动作。

items.en: Minister meant a servant or an attendant.
items.cn: minister 意为仆人或随从。

items.en: Ministrare meant to serve or to supply.
items.cn: ministrare 意为服务、供给。

items.en: With ad-, it meant to serve towards something, and so to manage it.
items.cn: 加上 ad- 后，意为朝某事物提供服务，因而引申为管理它。

items.en: English took it for running affairs and for giving remedies.
items.cn: 中世纪英语借入，用于处理事务与给予药物。

items.en: Law, government and medicine each kept a share of the word.
items.cn: 法律、政府与医学各自分得这个词的一部分。

note.en: The look-alike group is the administration family; the near-meaning group splits into managing and giving.
note.cn: 形近组是 administration 这一族；近义组分成「管理」与「给予」两条线。

entries.definition: Relating to management and paperwork.

entries.definition: To run an organization or team.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「管理、经营」，最通用。

entries.definition: To operate and control something day to day.

entries.definition: To give out medicine or goods to people.

normalIntro.en: The hooks start from the servant at the root and end at a nurse giving a vaccine.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从词根里的仆人开始，到一名护士接种疫苗结束。

normal.en: The Latin minister means servant, so administer is to serve towards a task, and therefore to run it.
normal.cn: 拉丁词 minister 意为仆人，所以 administer 是朝一项任务提供服务，因而就是管理它。

normal.en: Managing a charity, running a department and giving a drug all keep the service idea.
normal.cn: 管理慈善机构、掌管部门、给病人用药，都保留着「服务」这个想法。

normal.en: Administer justice means the court carries the law into effect.
normal.cn: administer justice 指法院把法律付诸实施。

normal.en: The noun administration covers both the activity and the people who do it.
normal.cn: 名词 administration 既指这项活动，也指做这件事的人。

normal.en: The word is formal; in everyday speech people manage or run things.
normal.cn: 这个词偏正式；日常口语里人们用 manage 或 run。

examples.cn: 她管理这个村的基金。

examples.cn: 护士在中午给了药。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: running affairs, putting rules into effect, and giving medicine.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：管理事务、施行规则、给予药物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person behind a desk assigning each task to a pair of hands.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在桌后，把每项任务分派给一双手。

branches.en: THE OFFICE: files and people are kept in order.
branches.cn: 办公室线：文件与人被维持得有条理。

branches.en: THE FUND: money is directed to where it is needed.
branches.cn: 基金线：钱被引向需要它的地方。

branches.en: THE COURT: a law is carried into effect.
branches.cn: 法院线：一条法律被落实到行动中。

branches.en: THE NURSE: a dose is measured and given.
branches.cn: 护士线：剂量被量好，然后给出。

branches.en: THE SERVICE: every use keeps the root idea of serving a task.
branches.cn: 服务线：每一种用法都保留着「为任务服务」这个词根意思。

intro.en: A Latin word for servant grew into a verb of serving, and English extended it to managing, enforcing and giving medicine.

latinIntro.cn: minister、ministrare 与 administrare 都有文献可证；英语词尾是后来加的。

senses.title: The work of managing
senses.definition: the process of managing the affairs of an organization
senses.definitionCN: 管理一个组织事务的过程
senses.example: Good administration keeps the office running smoothly.
senses.exampleCN: 良好的管理让办公室运转顺畅。
senses.why: The noun names the ongoing work of running something, not one decision.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指持续运转的管理工作，而不是某一次决定。

senses.title: The people who run it
senses.definition: the group of people who manage an organization or country
senses.definitionCN: 管理一个组织或国家的一群人
senses.example: The hospital administration approved the new ward.
senses.exampleCN: 医院行政部门批准了新病区。
senses.why: English commonly moves a noun from the activity to the people who carry it out.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把一个名词从活动本身转指执行这项活动的人。

senses.title: A government
senses.definition: a government, especially the team led by a president
senses.definitionCN: 政府，尤其指总统领导的那一届班子
senses.example: The administration promised to cut taxes.
senses.exampleCN: 这届政府承诺减税。
senses.why: American political usage narrowed the word to one governing team.
senses.whyCN: 美国的政治用法把这个词收窄到一届执政班子。

intro.en: administration is the noun of administer, and both trace back to the Latin word for a servant.
intro.cn: administration 是 administer 的名词，两者都能追到拉丁语里「仆人」这个词。

items.en: Minister meant a servant who attends to another.
items.cn: minister 意为在旁侍候的仆人。

items.en: Ministrare meant to serve or to supply what is needed.

items.cn: 这个名词先指活动，后来也指从事这项活动的一群人。

items.en: English used it for the conduct of public and private affairs.
items.cn: 中世纪英语用它指公共与私人事务的处理。

items.en: Politics fixed the sense of a governing team, and medicine kept the sense of giving a dose.
items.cn: 政治固定了「执政班子」的义项，医学保留了「给药」的义项。

note.en: The look-alike group is the administer family; the near-meaning group covers management and government.
